68adae322 · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 10, 14:43

Prototype: search and check a file's units in one process (--verify-units)

no-behaviour-change

Why

A unit's verdict takes two verifier processes: the search lowers the unit's slice, searches, checks its result, and writes the evidence; the check lowers the file, parses, translates and decodes that evidence, and checks it again. The command measures what one process over the file's one front costs.

addedTooling verifier --verify-units: a file's units searched and checked in one process

verifier --verify-units <mode> <ast> <claims> <file-key> <depth> [<names>]the file's plans built once; each selected group searched over thefile's own store and checked there; a verdict line per unit as`--check-units` prints it.mode 0: the group produced, then the unit's verdict at its encoded evidencemode 1: the group verified, the bundle checked as builtmode 2: the group verified, the search leaving the graph's check to        that checkA measuring prototype: the pipeline does not call it, and theacceptance theorem does not state its modes 1 and 2.

Validation

251a2bcff · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 10, 15:16

Prototype: a single forward pass over a unit's graph (--verify-units 3)

no-behaviour-change

Why

The search holds every fact at slots that each bind renumbers, so each node rewrites its whole knowledge. The pass names each binding once and keeps one store of facts over names, so a node touches only what its step reads.

addedDocs single-pass draft

stable names; one store indexed by name; one visit per node in a topological order of the graph without the edges into cuts; a cut's state its given invariant (written assertion and the claims' facts), every edge into it an obligation; the proved step rules applied to the facts over the names a step reads.

addedCheck the single pass: a unit's graph in one forward visit per node

at a stepthe proved step rule holds over the facts naming what the step reads, its derivation sought among those facts' types first
at an edge into a cutthe edge's state entails the cut's given invariant (its written assertion and the claims' facts) A measuring prototype: no certificate is built, the pipeline does not call it, and no theorem states it.

addedTooling verifier --verify-units, modes 3, 4 and 5

mode 3: the single pass; with TSCERT_COMPARE=1 each node's state is        checked to entail the knowledge the existing search's        certificate holds there.mode 4: the graph's shape statistics; mode 5: a node of the existing        search's certificate (TSCERT_NODE), for debugging.

Validation

measureAnalysis (pretext ba09794f), one run: mode 3 accepted, pass 1322 ms (mode 2 forward pass 4981 ms); 5844 nodes visited once, 1885 rule applications (140 over the whole store), 4099 reads named as their slot, 347 entailment queries (mean 32 facts); with TSCERT_COMPARE=1 every node's state entails the existing certificate's knowledge.

b4616e9ab · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 10, 21:47

Compute a unit's expression and binding types in one forward walk, and compare them to the claims

no-behaviour-change

Why

The end state has no producer: TScert computes the types the lowering reads. This first stage computes them beside the claims and measures the two against each other, construct by construct, before the lowering reads either.

addedProposal the walk: each expression's and binding's type, in one forward walk

one forward walk over a unit's fragment body in evaluation order:
literal ℓ
⇒its singleton type
parameter or annotated declaration
⇒its written type
identifier x
⇒x's binding's type narrowed by the tests on the path tests: truthiness, typeof and shape tests, strict equality with a one-value operand, discriminants, family guards
e.f, e[i]
⇒the field or position e's type states
f(a₁…aₙ)
⇒the result of the signature its actuals select generic: instantiated by matching each binder against the receiver and the actuals (a binder, an array of it, a function returning it) or at explicit type arguments
operator, comparison, c ? a : b, a ?? b, e!, cast
⇒the language's typing of the construct
let x = e
⇒x declared at e's type widened
[] assigned to a declared T
⇒T
[e₁…eₙ] as const
⇒a readonly tuple
loop head
⇒each binding the loop assigns at its declared type
merge
⇒the union of the arms' types
No search, fixed point or retry: what the rule does not determine is
recorded as undetermined with its reason.

Soundness

Untrusted: nothing reads the walk's types but the comparison.

addedTooling verifier --verify-units 7 and the type comparison script

mode 7: for each selected unit, the computed type against the claimedone at every expression occurrence and statement entry the claimsname: identical, wider, narrower, unrelated or undetermined, countedper construct kind, with each occurrence that is not identical.node dev/type-comparison.mts: the comparison over the pipeline cases,summed per construct kind.

Validation

  • growth-optional-accumulator-refused optionalAnnotated@290 agreement refused → verified pipeline refused: a safe gap program, reviewed
    // A key-adding write merges onto the local's object, typed by its annotation:
// a record of optional fields alone may be a host object, on which a merge is
// stuck (COMPILER-API.md, "Restricted values"). The object is the literal's,
// which the annotation does not say.
export function optionalAnnotated(): { a?: number } {
  const o: { a?: number } = {};
  o.a = 3;
  return o;
}
  • guarded-return captured@345 agreement verified → refused pipeline verified: a call ends a closure's captured narrowing
    // `if (x.f !== c) return x.f;`: the tested read is what the arm returns, in a
// function body and in a closure, through a `let` the closure captures.
export function direct(seed: boolean | null): boolean {
  let cell = { value: seed };
  cell = { value: null };
  if (cell.value !== null) return cell.value;
  return false;
}

export function captured(seed: boolean | null): boolean {
  let cell = { value: seed };
  const read = (): boolean => {
    if (cell.value !== null) return cell.value;
    return false;
  };
  cell = { value: null };
  return read();
}
  • json-parse-manifest text@588 agreement verified → refused pipeline verified: Array.isArray keeps the JSON dictionary arm
    // A manifest read from `JSON.parse` keeps its JSON type: a member is read
// after the tests that leave the dictionary arm, and a member's text is
// computed by the arms, as `String` converts it (`tools/files.mts`,
// `tools/family-activation.mts`).
type Json = null | boolean | number | string | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json };
export function member(
  manifest: Json,
  key: "name" | "version",
): Json | undefined {
  if (
    typeof manifest !== "object" ||
    manifest === null ||
    Array.isArray(manifest)
  )
    return undefined;
  return manifest[key];
}
export function text(value: Json): string {
  if (typeof value !== "object" || value === null) return String(value);
  if (Array.isArray(value))
    return value.map((x: Json) => (x === null ? "" : text(x))).join(",");
  if (Object.hasOwn(value, "toString"))
    throw new TypeError("Cannot convert object to primitive value");
  return "[object Object]";
}
export function version(source: string): string {
  const manifest: Json = JSON.parse(source);
  const found = member(manifest, "version");
  return found === undefined ? "" : text(found);
}
export function named(source: string, name: string): boolean {
  const manifest: Json = JSON.parse(source);
  return member(manifest, "name") === name;
}

    // A handler starts in the heap the throw left, after whatever the call
// wrote: a fact the guard before the call established of a field does not
// hold there. `clear` empties the field, then throws.
type Box = { v: string | undefined };
function clear(o: Box): number {
  o.v = undefined;
  throw Error("cleared");
}
export function wrong(o: Box): string {
  if (o.v === undefined) return "";
  try {
    clear(o);
  } catch {
    return o.v;
  }
  return "";
}

  op: "===" | "!==" | "==" | "!=",

  r: Expr,

    r: chainLeft ? other : body,

import type { Node } from "typescript/unstable/ast";

export function childOf(
  node: Node,
): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, Node | undefined> {
  if (ts.isBreakStatement(node)) return node.label;
  if (ts.isContinueStatement(node)) return node.label;
  if (ts.isLabeledStatement(node)) return node.label;
  return undefined;
}

export function childrenOf(
  node: Node,
): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, readonly Node[]> {
  if (ts.isFunctionDeclaration(node)) return node.parameters.filter(() => true);
  return [];
}

State each nested statement's entry at its own execution point

no-behaviour-change

Why

43 guards' own units were refused at their first edge, among them guard-boolean-return isList@625 (return Array.isArray(v);): "edge from node 12 to node 0". The parser reads a guard's Boolean return c as if (c) return true; else return false;, the if and the return true both starting at c's start. The walk kept one entry per start, so the if's execution point was given the return true's bindings, v already narrowed to Json[], which the start's edge does not establish. The implication rule the diagnosis proposed for these units is not needed: with each point at its own entry the existing promise check at the return accepts them.

modifiedProposal the claims-free front: an execution point's statement entry

Soundness

The entry is a proposal the pass checks on the edges into the point; the existing promise check at the return decides the guards. Each file's unsafe unit (shout, wrong, size) stays refused or not handled.

export type Presence = "dense" | "readable" | "sparse";

export function isPresence(value: unknown): value is Presence {
  return value === "dense" || value === "readable" || value === "sparse";

export function isText(x: string | number | null): x is string | null {
  if (typeof x === "string") return true;
  return x === null;
}

const isNumber = (v: unknown): v is number => typeof v === "number";

export function str(v: unknown): asserts v is string {
  if (typeof v !== "string") throw Error("expected a string");
}

function prefix(p: Presence): string {
  return p;
}

export function describe(v: unknown): string {
  if (isPresence(v)) return prefix(v);
  return isNumber(v) ? (v * 2).toString() : "none";
}

export function first(v: unknown): string {
  if (!isPresence(v)) return "none";
  return prefix(v);
}

export function small(a: unknown): boolean {
  return isNumber(a) && a < 1;
}

export function textLength(x: string | number | null): number {
  if (isText(x)) return x === null ? 0 : x.length;
  return -1;
}

  return v.length;
}

}

export function isWord(x: unknown): x is string {
  try {
    if (typeof x === "string") return true;
    throw Error("not a string");

    return false;

export function wordLength(v: unknown): number {
  return isWord(v) ? v.length : 0;

  return typeof x === "string";
}

export function boundLength(x: unknown): number {
  const guard = isLabel.bind(undefined);
  return guard(x) ? x.length : 0;
}

    // A loop updating a node to its grandparent through a branch a host guard
// refined: the update's entry has its own witness of `at.parent.parent`,
// whose chain of read links includes `at.parent`'s, and the branch's entry
// keeps both, so the update receives the loop test's links of both
// segments (HOST-FAMILIES.md, "Entries").
import * as ts from "typescript/unstable/ast";
export function use(node: ts.Node): boolean {
  let closure = false;
  for (
    let at: ts.Node = node;
    at.parent && at.parent.parent;
    at = at.parent.parent
  ) {
    if (ts.isFunctionLikeDeclaration(at)) closure = true;
  }
  return closure;
}

export function lineCount(text: string, keep: boolean): number {
  const lines = keep ? text.split("\n") : [];
  return lines.length;
}

  return cells.length;

export function aliasShrunk(text: string): number {
  const cells = text.split(",");
  const alias = cells;
  alias.pop();
  return cells.length;
}

export function annotated(text: string): number {
  const cells: string[] = text.split(",");
  return cells.length;
}

type Slots = { observation: string; result: string | null };
type Binder = { name: string; resolution: Slots | null };

function slots(name: string, resolvable: boolean): Slots {
  return {
    observation: `#observe:${name}`,
    result: resolvable ? `#resolve:${name}` : null,
  };

export function resolved(binder: Binder, resolvable: boolean): string | null {
  binder.resolution ??= slots(binder.name, resolvable);
  if (binder.resolution.result === null) return null;
  return binder.resolution.result;
}

}

  associated: (name: string) => Modifies<{ values: "any" }, string | null>;
};

export function scope(binders: (Binder & { span: number })[]): Scope {

    associated(name) {

      if (!binder) return null;
      binder.resolution ??= slots(binder.name, true);
      return binder.resolution.result;
    },
  };
}

  • comma-test-refinement cond agreement not handled → verified pipeline verified: a comma test
    // A comma in a test position (SOURCE-ELABORATION.md, "Derived source
// forms"): the left operand runs for its effects, then the right operand is
// the test, refining in the state the left one leaves, on both edges, in a
// condition, a conditional, and beside `&&`, `||` and `!`.
type A = { readonly kind: 1; readonly a: string };
type B = { readonly kind: 2; readonly b: string };
type C = { readonly kind: 3; readonly c: string };

export function cond(x: A | B | C): string {
  if ((x satisfies A | B | C, x.kind === 1 || x.kind === 2)) return x.kind === 1 ? x.a : x.b;
  return x.c;
}

export function ternary(x: A | B | C): string {
  return (x satisfies A | B | C, x.kind === 3) ? x.c : "";
}

export function conjunction(x: A | B | C): string {
  return (x satisfies A | B | C, x.kind === 3) && x.c ? x.c : "";
}

export function negation(x: A | B | C): string {
  return !(x satisfies A | B | C, x.kind !== 3) ? x.c : "";
}

export function counted(x: A | B | C): number {
  const box = { count: 0 };
  return (box.count++, x.kind === 1) ? box.count : -box.count;
}

// The test reads what the left operand wrote: `n` holds 5 when it runs.
export function written(): 5 | 0 {
  let n: number = 0;
  return (n = 5, n === 5) ? n : 0;
}

// A left operand that throws leaves the test unreached; the call's
// exception is the comma's.
const fail = (message: string): never => {
  throw new Error(message);
};

export function thrown(x: A | B | C): string {
  return (fail("left"), x.kind === 3) ? x.c : "";
}

// the test, refining in the state the left one leaves, on both edges, in a
// condition, a conditional, and beside `&&`, `||` and `!`.
type A = { readonly kind: 1; readonly a: string };
type B = { readonly kind: 2; readonly b: string };
type C = { readonly kind: 3; readonly c: string };

export function cond(x: A | B | C): string {
  if ((x satisfies A | B | C, x.kind === 1 || x.kind === 2)) return x.kind === 1 ? x.a : x.b;
  return x.c;
}

export function ternary(x: A | B | C): string {
  return (x satisfies A | B | C, x.kind === 3) ? x.c : "";
}

export function conjunction(x: A | B | C): string {
  return (x satisfies A | B | C, x.kind === 3) && x.c ? x.c : "";
}

export function negation(x: A | B | C): string {
  return !(x satisfies A | B | C, x.kind !== 3) ? x.c : "";
}

export function counted(x: A | B | C): number {
  const box = { count: 0 };
  return (box.count++, x.kind === 1) ? box.count : -box.count;
}

// The test reads what the left operand wrote: `n` holds 5 when it runs.
export function written(): 5 | 0 {
  let n: number = 0;
  return (n = 5, n === 5) ? n : 0;
}

// A left operand that throws leaves the test unreached; the call's
// exception is the comma's.
const fail = (message: string): never => {
  throw new Error(message);
};

export function thrown(x: A | B | C): string {
  return (fail("left"), x.kind === 3) ? x.c : "";
}

  • type-guards isPresence agreement refused → verified pipeline verified: an equality with a literal
    // A guard's promise is part of its function type, checked at its body and
// narrowing its argument where a call answers `true`: over a union of
// literals, of primitive kinds and of `null`, in a statement, a ternary, a
// conjunction and a negated early return; a module constant's arrow guard; a
// guard closure; a guard catching its own exception; an assertion function;
// a guard passed as a plain predicate; a guard bound with `.bind`, which keeps
// its promise about an actual it does not bind.
export type Presence = "dense" | "readable" | "sparse";

export function isPresence(value: unknown): value is Presence {
  return value === "dense" || value === "readable" || value === "sparse";
}

export function isText(x: string | number | null): x is string | null {
  if (typeof x === "string") return true;
  return x === null;
}

const isNumber = (v: unknown): v is number => typeof v === "number";

export function str(v: unknown): asserts v is string {
  if (typeof v !== "string") throw Error("expected a string");
}

function prefix(p: Presence): string {
  return p;
}

export function describe(v: unknown): string {
  if (isPresence(v)) return prefix(v);
  return isNumber(v) ? (v * 2).toString() : "none";
}

export function first(v: unknown): string {
  if (!isPresence(v)) return "none";
  return prefix(v);
}

export function small(a: unknown): boolean {
  return isNumber(a) && a < 1;
}

export function textLength(x: string | number | null): number {
  if (isText(x)) return x === null ? 0 : x.length;
  return -1;
}

export function length(v: unknown): number {
  str(v);
  return v.length;
}

export function predicate(): (v: unknown) => boolean {
  return isNumber;
}

export function size(v: unknown): number {
  const isString = (x: unknown): x is string => typeof x === "string";
  return isString(v) ? v.length : 0;
}

export function isWord(x: unknown): x is string {
  try {
    if (typeof x === "string") return true;
    throw Error("not a string");
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

export function wordLength(v: unknown): number {
  return isWord(v) ? v.length : 0;
}

function isLabel(x: unknown): x is string {
  return typeof x === "string";
}

export function boundLength(x: unknown): number {
  const guard = isLabel.bind(undefined);
  return guard(x) ? x.length : 0;
}
  • guard-footprint isPresence agreement refused → verified pipeline verified: an equality with a literal
    // A type guard and an assertion function claim the footprint their bodies
// stay within, as a plain declaration does: a `map` callback calling them
// keeps its result dense.
export type Presence = "dense" | "readable" | "sparse";
function isPresence(value: unknown): value is Presence {
  return value === "dense" || value === "readable" || value === "sparse";
}
function presence(value: unknown): asserts value is Presence {
  if (!isPresence(value)) throw Error("expected a presence");
}
export function presences(vs: (string | number)[]): boolean[] {
  return vs.map((v) => isPresence(v));
}
export function checked(vs: (string | number)[]): Presence[] {
  return vs.map((v): Presence => {
    presence(v);
    return v;
  });
}
// A guard adding to a set it is given writes the set's internal slots, not a
// store: its footprint keeps every dense prefix, and `map` stays dense.
function isText(v: string | number, seen: Set<string>): v is string {
  if (typeof v !== "string") return false;
  seen.add(v);
  return true;
}
export function texts(vs: (string | number)[], seen: Set<string>): boolean[] {
  return vs.map((v) => isText(v, seen));
}

    // A passed test against a string or a nonzero number leaves its operand that

export type Presence = "dense" | "readable" | "sparse";

export function presence(value: unknown): Presence | undefined {

  const p: "dense" | "sparse" = value;
  return p;
}

Give a class value the instance its constructor allocates, at its own keys

no-behaviour-change

Why

The single pass from the fragment (mode 8, verifier --verify-units 8) refused 72 class units the pipeline verifies. A subclass constructs its base through Base.[[class]] and copies the base instance's own fields into its own instance; the walk stated the class value with one construct signature, at the declared instance type, whose own keys are unknown, so the copy ({ ...Derived.[[base]] }) could not be stated at its exact keys and the derived constructor's code was refused (class-inheritance, class-static-inheritance). Error subclasses lower new Base(...)'s actuals and a later read of the base instance to expressions of one span in two statements, and the walk's one type per span gave the actual the read's type (error-subclass: parameter 0 claimed string). A class binding whose code is an earlier class binding's constructor (Base bound to Base.[[class]]'s lambda) walked that constructor again, as no fresh one, and replaced the allocation's type. An instance allocation was fitted at the declared instance type without its own-key bound, and its prototype link was read off a declared type that has none (nested-witness-optional-receiver).

Why

The walk stated a callback at its parameter's widest signature alone and a constant's literal at its own parameters alone, while a use passing it where a signature binding more parameters is expected needs that row: calls through it discard the extra actuals, and its body is checked at each row. Units of both shapes, a callback and a named constant's literal, were refused. The producer offers those rows.

    // A named closure whose parameter is wider than the element of the array it
// is passed to, here a union of which the element is one arm: it is offered
// the callback's longer signature at the element, and Lean checks its body
// there, the element within the closure's parameter.
type F = { k: "f"; n: number };
type A = { k: "a"; s: string };
type T = A | F;

export function visit(t: T): number {
  return t.k === "f" ? t.n : t.s.length;
}

export function each(calls: F[]): number {
  let total = 0;
  const go = (part: T): void => {
    total += visit(part);
  };
  calls.forEach(go);
  return total;
}

export function mapped(calls: F[]): string[] {
  const name = (t: T): string => t.k;
  return calls.map(name);
}

export function tested(calls: readonly F[]): boolean {
  const small = (t: T): boolean => visit(t) < 10;
  return calls.every(small) && calls.some(small);
}

// The element written inline, the parameter a written union of aliases.
export function inline(calls: { k: "f"; n: number }[]): number {
  let total = 0;
  const go = (part: A | F): void => {
    total += visit(part);
  };
  calls.forEach(go);
  return total;
}

// The element an alias of the union's arm, the parameter wider still.
type G = F;
export function widest(calls: G[]): string[] {
  const show = (v: T | null): string => (v === null ? "" : v.k);
  return calls.map(show);
}

// The closure changing storage: a captured array it pushes onto, and the
// mapped array itself, whose result is read with its holes.
export function collected(calls: F[]): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const add = (t: T): void => {
    out.push(t.k);
  };
  calls.forEach(add);
  return out;
}

export function shrinking(calls: F[]): (string | undefined)[] {
  const name = (t: T): string => {
    calls.pop();
    return t.k;
  };
  return calls.map(name);
}

// A guard closure wider than the element: `filter`'s guard overload.
export function present(calls: (F | null)[]): F[] {
  const isF = (t: T | null): t is F => t !== null && t.k === "f";
  return calls.filter(isF);
}

type JsonValue =
  | null
  | boolean
  | number
  | string
  | readonly JsonValue[]
  | { readonly [key: string]: JsonValue };
type Shown = {

interface Table {

const shown = (
  table: Table,

): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, Shown> => {
  const key = row === undefined ? "undefined" : JSON.stringify(row);
  const held = table.lifted.get(key);
  if (held !== undefined) return held;

      JsonValue[]

    atoms = later();

  table: Table,
  first: JsonValue | undefined,
  rest: readonly JsonValue[],
): JsonValue {
  const later = (
    row: JsonValue,
  ): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, Shown> => shown(table, row);

    // `f.call(r)` calls the standard `Function.prototype.call` where `f` is a
// known local function: every value of a local `let` (its initializer and
// each assignment) is one, and a member of an object built by a spread is the
// member its source holds. A closure captures the `let`.
type Reader = { value: number };

function readOwn(this: Reader): number {
  return this.value;
}

function captured(source: Reader): () => number {
  let alias: { read: (this: Reader) => number } = { read: readOwn };
  alias = { read: readOwn };
  return () => {
    const copy = { ...alias };
    return copy.read.call(source);
  };
}

function reassigned(source: Reader): number {
  let f = readOwn;
  f = function (this: Reader): number {
    return this.value + 1;
  };

    // A guard's false edge over an arm whose tag is a set (HOST-FAMILIES.md,
// "Calls"; PROGRAM-TYPING.md, "A membership test"): where `isToken` answers
// false, the `Token` arm of the set `DotToken | CommaToken`, all of which
// `isToken` accepts, is gone, so the node is the computed name; where
// `isDotToken` answers false, the same arm is read at its rest, a
// `CommaToken`, whose kind test then leaves the computed name too. Over
// `Node`, `isToken`'s false edge holds none of the arms of `Token`. The
// constant returns are the neighbours of `pipeline/test.mts`'s forged claims.
import * as ts from "typescript/unstable/ast";

type Punctuation = ts.Token<ts.SyntaxKind.DotToken | ts.SyntaxKind.CommaToken>;

export function nonToken(n: Punctuation | ts.ComputedPropertyName): number {
  if (ts.isToken(n)) return 0;
  return n.expression.pos;
}

export function afterDot(n: Punctuation | ts.ComputedPropertyName): number {
  if (ts.isDotToken(n)) return 0;
  if (n.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.CommaToken) return 1;
  return n.expression.pos;
}

export function anyNode(n: ts.Node): number {
  if (ts.isToken(n)) return 0;
  return n.pos;
}

export function nonTokenConstant(
  n: Punctuation | ts.ComputedPropertyName,
): number {
  if (ts.isToken(n)) return 0;
  return 1;
}

export function afterDotConstant(
  n: Punctuation | ts.ComputedPropertyName,
): number {
  if (ts.isDotToken(n)) return 0;
  return 1;
}

export function onTrue(n: Punctuation | ts.ComputedPropertyName): number {
  if (ts.isDotToken(n)) return n.pos;
  return 1;
}

    // A guard on a field holding an array beside null or a number, a `forEach`
// whose callback calls an imported function its module's run certifies at
// the empty footprint, then the field's reread: the callback keeps the heap,
// so the call keeps what the guard found. The twin of
// invalid-guard-field-unstated-callback-value-import, whose import states no
// effect.
import { twice } from "@fixture/certified";

type Value = null | number | readonly Value[];
type Row = { readonly context: Value };
export function count(t: Row, seen: Value, size: number): number {
  const labels = (v: Value) => twice(size);
  if (!Array.isArray(seen) || !Array.isArray(t.context)) return 0;
  seen.forEach(labels);
  t.context.forEach(labels);
  return t.context.length;
}

    // A test of a field narrows its reread after a `for...of` loop over an
// array: the iterator `%Iterate%` returns is a fresh object, separated from
// the fields of the records in scope, readonly views and writable fields
// alike, and each of its steps changes no old location but the iterator's
// own, so the read link of the tested field survives every step.
// Census functions: fragment-support.mts#forInEntryReads (its
// `declarations[0]` refusal is a consequence: the element `s` has no type).
type Statement = { k: "block"; statements: readonly number[] } | { k: "empty" };

export function count(node: { readonly statement: Statement }): number {
  if (node.statement.k !== "block") return 0;
  let n = 0;
  for (const s of node.statement.statements) n += s;
  return n + node.statement.statements.length;
}

}

import * as ts from "typescript/unstable/ast";
export function use(node: ts.ForInStatement): number {
  if (!ts.isBlock(node.statement)) return 0;

  }
  return node.statement.statements.length;

export function use(limit: number): {
  first(): number;
  second(): string;
} {
  return {
    first: () => {
      let i = 0;
      while (true) {
        if (i > limit) return i;
        i++;
      }

    second: () => {
      for (let i = 0, read = () => i; ; i++) {

      }
    },
  };

    // A memoizing lifter of JSON rows in the forms claim-text.mts writes it: each
// function states that it only grows the store, so `map` over a dense
// receiver keeps its result dense; the first, possibly absent, row is lifted
// apart from the rest, a JSON array whose elements are never absent; the
// lifted record states its index signature; the table's names are a native
// `Map`; a closure captures a tested name through a constant of the tested
// type.
// Census functions:
// claim-text.mts#liftClause
// claim-text.mts#liftSignatures
// claim-text.mts#liftType
// claim-text.mts#liftLabels
// claim-text.mts#treeAtom
// claim-text.mts#lift
type JsonValue =
  | null
  | boolean
  | number
  | string
  | readonly JsonValue[]
  | { readonly [key: string]: JsonValue };
type Shown = {
  readonly [key: string]: JsonValue;
  top: boolean;
  atoms: JsonValue[];
};
interface Table {
  names: Map<number, string>;
  lifted: Map<string, Shown>;
}
const shown = (
  table: Table,
  row: JsonValue | undefined,
): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, Shown> => {
  const key = row === undefined ? "undefined" : JSON.stringify(row);
  const held = table.lifted.get(key);
  if (held !== undefined) return held;
  const name = typeof row === "number" ? table.names.get(row) : undefined;
  let atoms: JsonValue[] = [typeof row];
  if (name !== undefined) {
    const named: string = name;
    const later = (): Modifies<
      { values: "any"; stores: "grow" },
      JsonValue[]
    > => [named];
    atoms = later();
  }
  const lifted: Shown = { top: false, atoms };
  table.lifted.set(key, lifted);
  return lifted;
};
export function liftAll(
  table: Table,
  first: JsonValue | undefined,
  rest: readonly JsonValue[],
): JsonValue {
  const later = (
    row: JsonValue,
  ): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, Shown> => shown(table, row);
  const cells = [shown(table, first), ...rest.map(later)];
  const [only] = cells;
  if (only === undefined || cells.length !== 1) return cells;
  return only;
}

export function grow(key: "x" | "y"): string {

Narrow a field's path by its logical assignment, and end a statement at a call returning never

no-behaviour-change

Why

Units refused where the pipeline verifies, which the walk did not handle before: field-write-refinement resolved (binder.resolution ??= slots(…), then binder.resolution.result) read the field at Slots | null: the walk ended the path at the write and stated nothing after it. read-narrows-path initializerWidth, measured and compiler-api-read-narrows-path initializerSpan (if (!d.initializer) fail("…"), fail returning never) joined the arm through the call, so d.initializer held undefined after it.

modifiedProposal the walk: a field's path after a logical assignment

modifiedProposal the walk: a statement whose value has no type

modifiedDocs single-pass.md, §9 narrowing and field contents

States both rules.

Soundness

The path's narrowing is to the assignment's value on the edge the write leaves, which the single pass checks as any stated path; the unreached rest is the arm mechanism the decided force's control exercises. Units newly accepted where the pipeline refuses: none.

  • field-write-refinement resolved agreement refused → verified pipeline verified: the path at the assignment's value
    // A field of an immutable binding's object holds what was last written to
// it until a call or another write: `x.f = v` and `x.f ??= v` leave the
// field at the written value's nullish exclusions, and a strict test of a
// path of two members refines its witness (HOST-FAMILIES.md, "Entries"), as
// type-term.mts's `quantified` caches a binder's resolution slots and reads
// their result.
type Slots = { observation: string; result: string | null };
type Binder = { name: string; resolution: Slots | null };

function slots(name: string, resolvable: boolean): Slots {
  return {
    observation: `#observe:${name}`,
    result: resolvable ? `#resolve:${name}` : null,
  };
}

// The cached slots' result, where the binder's resolution is resolvable.
export function resolved(binder: Binder, resolvable: boolean): string | null {
  binder.resolution ??= slots(binder.name, resolvable);
  if (binder.resolution.result === null) return null;
  return binder.resolution.result;
}

// A plain write, then a read of the field it wrote.
export function written(binder: Binder): Slots {
  binder.resolution = slots(binder.name, false);
  return binder.resolution;
}

// A path of two members tested against `null` in one statement and read in
// the next.
export function result(binder: { readonly resolution: Slots }): string {
  if (binder.resolution.result === null) return "";
  return binder.resolution.result;
}

// A method of a scope whose type states its effect, writing a field of a
// binder it finds, an intersection whose principal operand states the field:
// a named field's write changes a value's location, within the statement's
// footprint, as `quantified`'s `associated` does.
type Scope = {
  associated: (name: string) => Modifies<{ values: "any" }, string | null>;
};

export function scope(binders: (Binder & { span: number })[]): Scope {
  return {
    associated(name) {
      const binder = binders.find((b) => b.name === name);
      if (!binder) return null;
      binder.resolution ??= slots(binder.name, true);
      return binder.resolution.result;
    },
  };
}

class Gate {
  fail(node: ts.Node, message: string): never {
    throw new Error(`${message} at ${node.pos}`);
  }

export function initializerSpan(

  if (!d.initializer) gate.fail(d, "a `const` needs an initializer");

  • generic-closure-effect positive new → verified a generic closure's write, the field tested again after the call
    // A generic closure that writes the heap is claimed at an effect covering
// the write: its caller tests the written field again after the call.
export function reread(box: { value: number | null }): number {
  const reset = <T>(x: T): T => {
    box.value = null;
    return x;
  };
  if (box.value !== null) {
    const kept = reset(box.value);
    return box.value === null ? kept : box.value;
  }
  return 0;
}
  • invalid-generic-closure-effect negative new → refused the field returned as narrowed after the closure's write
    // A generic closure's write ends its caller's narrowing of the field it
// writes: after the call the field holds `null`, which the function returns
// where it promises a number.
export function stale(box: { value: number | null }): number {
  const reset = <T>(x: T): T => {
    box.value = null;
    return x;
  };
  if (box.value !== null) {
    reset(0);
    return box.value;
  }
  return 0;
}

  • map-stable-fresh-store heads agreement disagreed → verified pipeline verified: the change counted at the instance's footprint
    // `map` callbacks removing from arrays they allocated: through a constant
// whose code returns `filter`'s fresh result, from `split` and from `map`.
// `shift`, `pop` and `reverse` change only their receiver's store beside
// element contents, and each receiver's store was allocated after the
// callback began, so each callback is within `{value: any, store: keep}`
// and every result is dense.
const parts = (line: string): string[] =>
  line
    .trim()
    .split(/\s{3,}/)
    .filter(Boolean);
const same = (a: string[]): string[] => a;

export function heads(lines: string[]): string[] {
  return lines.map((l) => {
    const rest = parts(l);
    return rest.shift() ?? "";
  });
}

export function lasts(lines: string[]): string[] {
  return lines.map((l) => {
    const cells = l.split(",");
    const copy = cells;
    return copy.pop() ?? "";
  });
}

export function backwards(lines: string[]): string[] {
  return lines.map((l) => {
    const widths = l.split(",").map((c) => c.length);
    widths.reverse();
    return widths.join(",");
  });
}

export function sizes(lines: string[]): number[] {
  return lines.map((l) => same(parts(l)).length);
}

Control a function literal's default effect

no-behaviour-change
closure-default-effect.ts#rereadinvalid-closure-default-effect.ts#stale

Why

A function literal's defaults run at a call omitting their arguments, so their effect is the literal's (the walk walks them at its entry, 8a623a5e), but no case held a function literal of no written effect whose default changes the heap, and no control showed a proposal leaving that change out is refused.

defaults

closure-default-effect reread@279unforced accepted → forced refused at the literal's footprint ("code 0: footprint at node 1")

modifiedDocs single-pass.md, §9 "Function literals", §8 the controls

States the forced proposal and its control.

Effect

  • closure-default-effect positive new → verified a default's write, the field tested again after the call
    // A function literal of no written effect whose parameter default writes a
// field its caller narrowed: the default runs at a call omitting its
// argument, so the literal's effect is its default's write, and the caller
// tests the field again after the call.
export function reread(box: { value: number | null }): number {
  const read = (n: number, reset: null = (box.value = null)): number => n;
  if (box.value !== null) {
    const kept = read(box.value);
    return box.value === null ? kept : box.value;
  }
  return 0;
}
  • invalid-closure-default-effect negative new → refused the field returned as narrowed after a call running the default
    // A function literal of no written effect whose parameter default writes a
// field its caller narrowed: a call omitting the argument runs the default,
// after which the field holds `null`, which the caller returns where it
// promises a number.
export function stale(box: { value: number | null }): number {
  const read = (n: number, reset: null = (box.value = null)): number => n;
  if (box.value !== null) {
    read(0);
    return box.value;
  }
  return 0;
}

Effect

  • try-catch cleanup agreement refused → verified pipeline verified: the finalizer's entry joins its routes
    // `try`: a throw may come from any point of the body, so the handler and the
// finalizer start from the cells' contracts, not from what the body wrote;
// the caught value is `unknown`, and a `typeof` test narrows it. A `throw`
// leaves the function unless a `try` catches it; the `finally` block runs on
// every way out, a `return` included, which then resumes.
function recover(mayThrow: () => void): number {
  let y: number | null = 1;
  try {
    y = 2;
    mayThrow();
  } catch (e) {
    const caught: unknown = e;
    y = 0;
  }
  if (y === null) {
    return -1;
  }
  return y;
}

function cleanup(mayThrow: () => void): boolean {
  let done: boolean = false;
  try {
    mayThrow();
  } finally {
    done = true;
  }
  return done;
}

function both(mayThrow: () => void): number {
  let y: number = 0;
  try {
    mayThrow();
    y = 1;
  } catch {
    y = 2;
  } finally {
    y = y + 1;
  }
  return y;
}

function returnsFromHandler(mayThrow: () => number): number {
  try {
    return mayThrow();
  } catch (e: unknown) {
    return 0;
  }
}

function raise(x: number | null): number {
  if (x === null) {
    throw "no value";
  }
  return x;
}

function handled(x: number | null): number {
  try {
    if (x === null) {
      throw x;
    }
    return x;
  } catch {
    return 0;
  }
}

function describe(f: () => string): string {
  try {
    return f();
  } catch (e) {
    if (typeof e === "string") {
      return e;
    }
    return "unknown";
  }
}

function rethrow(f: () => number): number {
  try {
    return f();
  } catch (e) {
    throw e;
  }
}

function returnThroughFinally(
  f: () => number,
  log: (n: number) => void,
): number {
  let seen: number = 0;

    return f();
  } finally {
    log(seen);
  }
}

function nested(f: () => number, g: () => void): number {
  try {
    try {
      return f();
    } finally {
      g();
    }
  } catch {
    return -1;
  }
}

function finallyOverrides(f: () => number): number {
  try {
    return f();
  } finally {
    return 0;
  }
}

async function awaited(p: Promise<number>): Promise<number> {
  try {
    return await p;
  } catch {
    return 0;
  }
}

function links(f: () => number, o: { a: number }): number {
  let c: number = 0;
  try {
    c = f();
    o.a = c;
  } catch (e) {
    c = o.a;
  } finally {
    o.a = 1;
  }
  return c;
}

function loopTry(xs: number[], f: (n: number) => number): number {
  let total: number = 0;
  for (const x of xs) {
    try {
      total = total + f(x);
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
  }
  return total;
}

    // A guard's Boolean return, at its boundaries: the test runs once, its
// effects and its throws as written; a `finally` runs after the returned
// answer is fixed, and one that returns overrides it; a closure inside a
// guard returns its own value, and a guard inside a closure returns its
// truth; an arrow guard with a defaulted parameter.
type Json = null | boolean | number | string | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json };
export function counted(v: Json, log: string[]): v is string {
  return typeof v === "string" && log.push("tested") > 0;
}
function check(v: string): boolean {
  if (v === "") throw Error("empty");
  return true;
}
export function nonEmpty(v: Json): v is string {
  return typeof v === "string" && check(v) === true;
}
export function finished(v: Json, log: string[]): v is string {
  try {
    return typeof v === "string";
  } finally {
    log.push("finally");
  }
}
export function overridden(v: Json): v is string {
  try {
    return typeof v === "string";
  } finally {
    return false;
  }
}
export function nested(v: Json): v is string {
  const positive = (n: number): boolean => n > 0;
  return typeof v === "string" && positive(v.length) === true;
}
export function guardOf(): (v: Json) => v is number {
  return (v: Json): v is number => typeof v === "number";
}
export const atLeast = (v: Json, min: number = 0): v is number =>
  typeof v === "number" && v >= min;

    // A call of a function declared to return `never` returns normally into no
// environment: after `if (…) fail(…)` the next statement is reached by the
// condition's `false` edge alone, and sees its refinement. A call returning
// a value continues as any call does.
function fail(message: string): never {
  throw new Error(message);
}

function warn(message: string): void {
  if (message.length > 1000) throw new Error("long");
}

export function checked(x: string | number): string {
  if (typeof x !== "string") fail("not a string");
  return x;
}

export function bound(x: string | number): string {
  const never = typeof x === "string" ? x : fail("not a string");
  return never;
}

// The statement after the call is reached by no edge: its bindings are
// claimed at the empty type.
export function unreached(x: number): number {
  fail("always");
  return x;
}

// The call's throw still reaches the handler and the `finally` block: only
// its normal return is never taken.
export function caught(x: string | number): string {
  let seen = "start";
  try {
    if (typeof x !== "string") fail("not a string");
    seen = x;
  } catch {
    seen = typeof x === "number" ? "caught" : "thrown";
  } finally {
    seen = seen + "!";
  }
  return seen;
}

export function warned(x: string | number): string {
  if (typeof x !== "string") warn("not a string");
  return typeof x === "string" ? x : "";
}

    // A method typed `never` that shrinks the array it is handed, then throws,
// called in a `map` callback that catches the throw: the call never returns
// normally, but its throw reaches the handler, and the method's signature
// bounds no heap on a throw. The result may hold holes and is not
// `number[]` (run under Node: `map` skips the index the method removed).
export class Bump {
  bump(xs: number[]): never {
    xs.pop();
    throw new Error("bumped");
  }
}

export function wrong(b: Bump, xs: number[]): number[] {
  const r: number[] = xs.map((x) => {
    try {
      b.bump(xs);
    } catch {
      return x;
    }
  });
  return r;
}
  • invalid-node-process-exit-handler rows agreement not handled → refused pipeline refused
    // `process.exit` runs the `exit` listeners synchronously, and one may change
// the array `map` reads and then throw into the caller (run under Node: the
// handler goes on and the result has a hole): the call states no effect, on
// its throw too.
export function rows(xs: number[]): number[] {
  return xs.map((x) => {
    try {
      process.exit(0);
    } catch {
      return x;
    }
  });
}
  • try-finally-jump switchThroughFinally agreement refused → not handled pipeline verified: as the pass over the producer's claims decides it
    // A `break` or `continue` leaving a `try` runs its `finally` on the way,
// innermost first, each in its `try`'s context, then lands; a `finally`
// that jumps itself leaves by its own way.
export function breakThroughFinally(xs: number[]): number {
  let count = 0;
  for (const x of xs) {
    try {
      if (x < 0) {
        break;
      }
      count = count + 1;
    } finally {
      count = count * 2;
    }
  }
  return count;
}

export function continueThroughTwo(xs: number[]): number {
  let n = 0;
  for (const x of xs) {
    try {
      try {
        if (x > 0) continue;
        n = n + 1;
      } finally {
        n = n + 2;
      }
    } finally {
      n = n + 3;
    }
  }
  return n;
}

export function switchThroughFinally(k: number): "a" | "b" {
  let x: "a" | "b" = "a";
  switch (k) {
    case 1:
      try {
        break;
      } finally {
        x = "b";
      }
    default:
      x = "a";
  }
  return x;
}

export function exitState(n: number): "b" {
  let x: "a" | "b" = "a";
  let i = 0;
  while (i < n) {
    i = i + 1;
    try {
      x = "a";
      break;
    } finally {
      x = "b";
    }
  }
  if (x === "a") return "b";
  return x;
}

export function jumpFromCatch(c: () => boolean, mayThrow: () => void): number {
  let n = 0;
  while (c()) {
    try {
      mayThrow();
    } catch {
      break;
    } finally {
      n = 1;
    }
  }
  return n;
}

export function finallyOverridesJump(c: () => boolean): number {
  while (c()) {
    try {
      break;
    } finally {
      return 1;
    }
  }
  return 0;
}

    // A `finally` block runs after the `continue` it encloses: there, the
// binding may be the spread the test answered `true` of (run under Node).
import * as ts from "typescript/unstable/ast";

export function names(o: ts.ObjectLiteralExpression): ts.PropertyName[] {
  const out: ts.PropertyName[] = [];
  for (const p of o.properties) {
    try {
      if (ts.isSpreadAssignment(p)) continue;
    } finally {
      out.push(p.name);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

Gap

try-catch both, try-finally-jump exitState, jumpFromCatch, finallyOverridesJump and switchThroughFinally stay not handled, and the pass over the producer's claims (mode 3) does not decide them either: a finalizer's throw copy that no throw reaches is a node no path from the start reaches whose context some environment meets. The lowering fixes a handler's %thrown@…% binding at unknown (lean/Verification/Source/Lowering/Flow.lean:133) whatever the claims state (the producer states it at the empty type), and the pass declines such a node (lean/Verification/Programs/SinglePass.lean:1782-1787); deciding them needs the pass to check an unreached node at its own context, or the lowering to take the handler binding's claimed type. The cause is in the pass and the lowering, not the walk.

Effect

  • type-parameter-meet-narrowing present agreement refused → verified pipeline verified: the meet sliced by the test
    // A test keeps a type parameter's value within its bound's values the test
// admits: the meet of the parameter with them, still a `T`.

// `x ?? d` takes `x` where it is neither null nor undefined: `T ⊓ number`.
export function present<T extends number | null | undefined>(x: T): number {
  return x ?? 0;
}

export function presentString<T extends string | null>(x: T): string | number {
  return x ?? 0;
}

export function presentEither<T extends number | string | null>(
  x: T,
): string | number {
  return x ?? 0;
}

// No value of the bound is other than null or undefined.
export function absent<T extends null | undefined>(x: T): number {

Keep a stable member's path across a call, narrow a field by its write, and type pattern parts

no-behaviour-change

Why

compiler-api-stable-optional initializerOf and clauseExpression, compiler-api-stable-link nameText and operandText, compiler-api-slot-path keyAfterCall: a compiler-API node's field narrowed by a test (if (!d.initializer) fail(d)) was ended by a later call of a parameter (log(d.initializer)), where the producer keeps a path through members its receiver states stable, which no step writes. field-write-refinement written and blocker-pretext-sibling-field-write wholeRunContext: after o.f = v the field was read at its contract (Slots | null), not at the value written. destructuring swap ([p, q] = [q, p]) made the literal at number[], which a pattern reads with undefined; pattern-array-rest-slice optionalRest read the rest of [number, string?] without undefined.

modifiedProposal the walk: a narrowed path across a call

stable_path through stable_member, ocaml-producer/refinement.ml:195-251; written_field, ocaml-producer/statement_analysis.ml:168-172, 419; slice_element, ocaml-producer/type_queries.ml:626-638.

States the four rules.

Soundness

Each is a proposal the single pass checks: a kept or written path as any stated path (the existing paths forced proposal, which keeps every narrowed path at every later statement, and its controls invalid-slot-path-call keyText and invalid-path-witness-alias wrong stay refused), the tuple and the rest's element at the allocation and the call they type. The negative cases of these families (invalid-compiler-api-stable-mixed, -record, -let, -catch, -let-cell, invalid-slot-path-*, invalid-path-witness-*, invalid-read-narrows-*) stay refused. Units newly accepted where the pipeline refuses: none.

  • compiler-api-stable-optional initializerOf agreement refused → verified pipeline verified: a stable member's path kept
    // An optional member of a node's shape tested and read again past calls
// (HOST-FAMILIES.md, "Stable keys"): an optional member is fixed when the
// node is built, present with one value or absent, so the read link from
// the test's read survives every call, absent or present. `initializerOf`
// is the shape of `patternStmt` in `tools/fragment-statements.mts`: a test
// that leaves on absence, calls, and the member read as present.
import * as ts from "typescript/unstable/ast";

export function initializerOf(
  d: ts.VariableDeclaration,
  fail: (n: ts.Node) => never,
  log: (n: ts.Node) => void,
): ts.Expression {
  if (!d.initializer) fail(d);
  log(d.initializer);
  log(d);
  return d.initializer;
}

export function initializerKind(
  d: ts.VariableDeclaration,
  log: () => void,
): number {
  return d.initializer ? (log(), d.initializer.kind) : 0;
}

export function noInitializer(
  d: ts.VariableDeclaration,
  log: (n: ts.Node) => void,
): undefined {
  if (d.initializer) return undefined;
  log(d);
  return d.initializer;
}

// A corrected member, declared required and absent at run time:
// `DefaultClause.expression`, read as optional.
export function clauseExpression(
  c: ts.CaseOrDefaultClause,
  log: () => void,
): ts.Expression | null {
  if (!ts.isDefaultClause(c)) return null;
  if (!c.expression) return null;
  log();
  return c.expression;
}

const UNCLOSABLE = "an array pattern over an iterator that cannot be closed";

export class Gate {

  if (d.type) gate.fail(d, "an annotated pattern is outside the fragment");
  if (!d.initializer) gate.fail(d, "a `const` needs an initializer");

      !d.name.elements.some((e) => ts.isBindingElement(e) && e.dotDotDotToken)

  }

}

    // `instanceof Map` and `instanceof Set` on a value of unknown type, the
// collection then iterated, and the value a key of a map read by `has` and
// `get`.
export function copied(value: unknown, seen: Map<object, unknown>): unknown {
  if (!value || typeof value !== "object") return value;
  if (seen.has(value)) return seen.get(value);
  if (value instanceof Map) {
    const result = new Map<unknown, unknown>();
    seen.set(value, result);
    for (const [key, item] of value) result.set(key, copied(item, seen));
    return result;
  }
  if (value instanceof Set) {
    const result = new Set<unknown>();
    seen.set(value, result);
    for (const item of value) result.add(copied(item, seen));
    return result;
  }
  return value;
}

class Draining {
  constructor(readonly items: number[]) {}

    const items = this.items;

    // The default is universally valid, but its input contract needs T | undefined
// in the rigid claim/certificate language; replacing T with its bound is wrong.
function rigidDefault(seed: boolean): boolean {
  const pick = <T>(value: T, copy: T = value): T => copy;
  return pick(seed);
}

// T may itself contain undefined. Initialization must not narrow T by deleting
// undefined from the instantiated input type.
function undefinedRigidDefault(seed: boolean | undefined): boolean | undefined {
  const pick = <T>(value: T, copy: T = value): T => copy;
  return pick(seed);
}

// Forward capture and a rigid default share the same initialization schedule.
function genericDeferredDefault(seed: boolean): boolean {
  const pick = <T>(
    value: T,
    read: () => T = (): T => later,
    later: T = value,
  ): T => read();
  return pick(seed);
}

// A call cannot reach the slot: `y` is still "a" where the call throws.
export function survivesCall(a: "a", b: "b", mayThrow: () => void): "a" {
  let y: "a" | "b" = a;
  y = b;
  y = a;
  try {
    mayThrow();
  } catch {
    return y;
  }
  return y;
}

// outer catch is entered from the second call alone, with `y` at "a".

  let y: "a" | "b" = a;
  try {
    try {
      y = b;
      mayThrow();
      y = a;
    } catch {
      y = a;
    }

  } catch {
    return y;
  }
  return y;

    // A decoder of parsed JSON returns fresh storage built from the values it
// checked: a list of in-bounds numbers, each element tested as `map` visits
// it, and a record of a Boolean and such a list, each field tested where it
// is read (`decodeLabels` and `decodeGraph` of `tools/type-graph.mts`,

// parsed value leaves the decoded one as it was.
type Json = null | boolean | number | string | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json };
type JsonValue =
  | null
  | boolean
  | number
  | string
  | readonly JsonValue[]
  | { readonly [key: string]: JsonValue };
type JsonObject = { readonly [key: string]: JsonValue };
type Decoded = { top: boolean; labels: number[] };
const isList = (v: JsonValue | undefined): v is readonly JsonValue[] =>
  Array.isArray(v);
const isRecord = (v: JsonValue | undefined): v is JsonObject =>
  typeof v === "object" && v !== null && !Array.isArray(v);
export function decode(v: JsonValue | undefined, size: number): number[] {
  if (!isList(v)) throw Error("expected a list");
  return v.map((i) => {
    if (typeof i !== "number" || i < 0 || i >= size)
      throw Error("reference out of bounds");
    return i;
  });
}
export function decodeRecord(v: JsonValue | undefined, size: number): Decoded {
  if (!isRecord(v) || Object.keys(v).length !== 2)
    throw Error("expected a record");
  const top = v.top;
  if (typeof top !== "boolean") throw Error("expected a boolean");
  return { top, labels: decode(v.labels, size) };
}
export function first(text: string): number | undefined {
  const parsed: Json = JSON.parse(text);
  const labels = decode(parsed, 2);
  if (Array.isArray(parsed)) parsed[0] = "x";
  return labels[0];
}
export function flag(text: string): boolean {
  const parsed: Json = JSON.parse(text);
  const decoded = decodeRecord(parsed, 2);
  decoded.labels.push(1);
  return decoded.top;
}

    // A closure's assigned parameter that no closure writes, and no closure
// created before one of its writes mentions, is a slot of the closure's
// activation, as a function's is: a test of the object it holds narrows it
// until the next write, which rebinds it at what it writes.

type Expr =
  | { kind: "paren"; inner: Expr }
  | { kind: "name"; text: string }
  | { kind: "call"; callee: Expr; args: Expr[] };

const isParen = (e: Expr): e is Extract<Expr, { kind: "paren" }> =>
  e.kind === "paren";

// A tag test in a loop's condition, the write in its body: each iteration's
// test narrows what the previous write stored.
export const unwrap = (e: Expr): Expr => {
  while (e.kind === "paren") e = e.inner;
  return e;
};

// A user guard, then tests after the loop; a recursive closure.
export function names(root: Expr): string[] {
  const found: string[] = [];
  const visit = (e: Expr): void => {
    while (isParen(e)) e = e.inner;
    if (e.kind === "name") found.push(e.text);
    else if (e.kind === "call") {
      visit(e.callee);
      e.args.forEach((a) => visit(a));
    }
  };
  visit(root);
  return found;
}

// A test, then a write of one arm, read at that arm.
type Shape =
  | { kind: "circle"; radius: number }
  | { kind: "square"; side: number };
export const area = (s: Shape): number => {
  if (s.kind === "circle") return 3 * s.radius * s.radius;
  s = { kind: "square", side: s.side * 2 };
  return s.side;
};

// A closure created after the last write reads the value it captured.
export const later = (e: Expr): (() => string) => {
  while (e.kind === "paren") e = e.inner;
  if (e.kind !== "name") return () => "";
  return () => e.text;
};

    // Store-preserving splitting keeps mapped arms readable through reduction
// and iteration before flatMap calls each element's function.
// Census functions:
// claim-text.mts#liftClause
// claim-text.mts#liftSignatures
// claim-text.mts#liftType
// claim-text.mts#liftLabels
// claim-text.mts#treeAtom
// claim-text.mts#lift
type Arm = { count: number; lift: (limit?: number) => string[] };
export function lift(
  labels: readonly string[],
  limit: number,
  split: (s: string) => Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, string[]>,
): string[] {
  const armOf = (
    label: string,
  ): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, Arm> => {
    const clauses = split(label);
    return {
      count: clauses.length,
      lift: (limit) => clauses.slice(0, limit).map((clause) => clause),
    };
  };
  const arms = labels.map(armOf);
  const total = arms.reduce((n, arm) => n + arm.count, 0);
  if (total > limit) {
    const atoms: string[] = [];
    for (const arm of arms) {
      if (atoms.length >= limit) break;
      atoms.push(...arm.lift(limit - atoms.length));
    }
    return atoms;
  }
  return arms.flatMap((arm) => arm.lift());
}

type Span = [start: number, end: number];
type E =
  | { k: "lit"; pos: Span; v: string }

export function template(

Propose a declared function's footprint at the grades its walk finds

no-behaviour-change

Why

A function of the file without a written effect was proposed a footprint only where its walk changed nothing at all; any write, and any call passing a function, left it at the ordinary effect. A caller then lost its length, cursor and field facts across the call, where the producer's inferred footprint keeps them: 26 units the pipeline verifies were refused, each accepted with the producer's footprint as a stand-in. Guard and assertion functions were left out altogether.

type ObjectTerm = Extract<TypeTerm, { k: "object" }>;

    // A closure's assigned parameter that no closure writes, and no closure
// created before one of its writes mentions, is a slot of the closure's
// activation, as a function's is: a test of the object it holds narrows it
// until the next write, which rebinds it at what it writes.

type Expr =
  | { kind: "paren"; inner: Expr }
  | { kind: "name"; text: string }
  | { kind: "call"; callee: Expr; args: Expr[] };

const isParen = (e: Expr): e is Extract<Expr, { kind: "paren" }> =>
  e.kind === "paren";

// A tag test in a loop's condition, the write in its body: each iteration's
// test narrows what the previous write stored.
export const unwrap = (e: Expr): Expr => {
  while (e.kind === "paren") e = e.inner;
  return e;
};

// A user guard, then tests after the loop; a recursive closure.
export function names(root: Expr): string[] {
  const found: string[] = [];
  const visit = (e: Expr): void => {
    while (isParen(e)) e = e.inner;
    if (e.kind === "name") found.push(e.text);
    else if (e.kind === "call") {
      visit(e.callee);
      e.args.forEach((a) => visit(a));
    }
  };
  visit(root);
  return found;
}

// A test, then a write of one arm, read at that arm.
type Shape =
  | { kind: "circle"; radius: number }
  | { kind: "square"; side: number };
export const area = (s: Shape): number => {
  if (s.kind === "circle") return 3 * s.radius * s.radius;
  s = { kind: "square", side: s.side * 2 };
  return s.side;
};

// A closure created after the last write reads the value it captured.
export const later = (e: Expr): (() => string) => {
  while (e.kind === "paren") e = e.inner;
  if (e.kind !== "name") return () => "";
  return () => e.text;
};

    // A write of `true` fits the `null | boolean` arm of the cell's union but not
// the arm holding only `null`: the cell may be of that arm, so the write's
// obligation fails, though TypeScript admits it.

type Cell = { value: null | boolean } | { value: null };

function writeTrue(): null | boolean {
  const cell: Cell = { value: null };
  const touch = (unit: null): null | boolean => {
    cell.value = true;
    return cell.value;
  };
  return touch(null);
}

export function copy(): { own: number; two: number } {

The empty type is stated only where the walk's state is unreached (a statement after a call of no value, an arm a test leaves a binding no value): the node's context is then unsatisfiable, and an edge into it from a reached node is checked by the single pass against it.     // A `map` callback whose only program call is one typed `never` at its
// instance: the call never returns normally, so on normal return it changes
// nothing, the callback is within the empty footprint and the result is
// dense. The call is a class member's, a generic function's instance at
// `never`, and a function's with a rest parameter, none of whose signatures
// states an effect a `map` callback could use.
export class Gate {
  prefix: string = "";
  fail(message: string): never {
    throw new Error(this.prefix + message);
  }
}

export function members(gate: Gate, xs: string[]): string[] {
  const r: string[] = xs.map((x) => {
    if (x === "") return gate.fail("empty");
    return x;
  });
  return r;
}

function die<T>(message: string): T {
  throw new Error(message);
}

export function instances(xs: number[]): number[] {
  const r: number[] = xs.map((x) => {
    if (x < 0) return die<never>("negative");
    return x;
  });
  return r;
}

function failAll(...parts: string[]): never {
  throw new Error(parts.join(" "));
}

export function rests(xs: string[]): string[] {
  const r: string[] = xs.map((x) => {
    if (x === "") return failAll("empty", "string");
    return x;
  });
  return r;
}

// An async function and an async arrow whose bodies reach no completion: a
// call of the never-returning `stop`, then a throw. An async call returns
// its promise where its body throws, so each verifies at the footprint
// letting every location change, as every async definition does.
export async function rejected(
  xs: number[],
  stop: (xs: number[]) => never,
): Promise<number> {
  stop(xs);
  throw new Error("unreached");
}

export function rejecting(): (
  xs: number[],
  stop: (xs: number[]) => never,
) => Promise<number> {
  return async (
    ys: number[],
    stop: (ys: number[]) => never,
  ): Promise<number> => {
    stop(ys);
    throw new Error("unreached");
  };
}

// An async recursive constant whose body reaches no completion: it calls
// itself, then the never-returning `stop`, then throws. It verifies at the
// footprint letting every location change.
export const countdown = async (
  n: number,
  stop: (n: number) => never,
): Promise<number> => {
  if (n > 0) countdown(n - 1, stop);
  stop(n);
  throw new Error("unreached");
};

    // An async function whose body reaches no completion: it calls a
// never-returning callee, then throws. Its graph is a synchronous body's,
// and its throw rejects the promise its call returns, so its footprint is
// `top` (run under Node: the callee pops synchronously, and `map` skips the
// index it removed).
function fail(xs: number[]): never {
  xs.pop();
  throw new Error("failed");
}

async function run(
  xs: number[],
  stop: (xs: number[]) => never,
): Promise<number> {
  stop(xs);
  throw new Error("unreached");
}

export function wrong(xs: number[]): number[] {
  const r: number[] = xs.map((x) => {
    run(xs, fail);
    return x;
  });
  return r;
}

    // A `switch` whose `case` labels are enum members narrows as the same test

// selects, `default` the rest, for a name and a field of a name, a
// `const enum`'s members too, and a `default` written between cases
// (`switch-enum-value-import` for an imported enum).
const enum C {
  Red = "red",
  Blue = "blue",
}
type R = { readonly c: C.Red; readonly r: number };
type U = { readonly c: C.Blue; readonly u: number };

export function middleDefault(v: R | U): number {
  switch (v.c) {
    case C.Red:
      return v.r;
    default:
      return v.u;
    case C.Blue:
      return v.u;
  }
}

enum K {
  One = 1,
  Two = 2,
}
type A = { readonly kind: K.One; readonly a: string };
type B = { readonly kind: K.Two; readonly b: string };

export function read(n: A | B): string {
  switch (n.kind) {
    case K.One:
      return n.a;
    default:
      return n.b;
  }
}

export function both(k: K): 1 | 2 {
  switch (k) {
    case K.One: {
      const one: K.One = k;
      return one;
    }
    case K.Two: {
      const two: K.Two = k;
      return two;
    }
  }
}

raw.replace(/…/g, (_: string, point: unknown, unit: unknown) => …) was refused at the invoke of the callback in [Symbol.replace]'s contract. A string's replace dispatching to a native regex states its callback parameter as a binder F the regex parameter's [Symbol.replace](string, F) also takes; the walk read F off the literal alone, its own row, where the producer first seeds F with the replacer the regex's [Symbol.replace] takes at that position, walks the literal there, and so states it also at the replacer's longer row (whole match, captures, position, input).

The literal at each row it is stated at is a code request whose signature and graph the unit's check passes before the code is admitted (lean/Verification/Source/Claims/Json.lean:994-1048), and the call passes the regex where { [Symbol.replace](string, F) } is expected with F the literal's type, which the single pass checks at the call (lean/Verification/Programs/SinglePass.lean:1260): a row wider in its parameters than the regex's replacer is not within it. No forced-proposal control added.

The module-constant extension of the previous commit (a rest of unknown, stated for every such unannotated constant, where the producer states it for one read as a value somewhere) can make a unit accepted that the producer's choice refuses: one calling the constant by name with more actuals than its parameters (TypeScript's excess-argument error, which TScert does not refuse on). Such a unit is safe: the extended row is a code request checked as above, its code discarding the further actuals after the caller evaluates them. None occurs among the pipeline cases. Kept as stated.

    // A replacement callback a native regex's `[Symbol.replace]` calls: the
// whole match, each capture (a string where the group takes part in every
// match, else maybe `undefined`), the position, the input, and the `groups`
// object where a group is named. Its parameters may be fewer or wider.
export function decode(raw: string): string {
  return raw.replace(
    /\\u\{([0-9A-Fa-f]+)\}|\\u([0-9A-Fa-f]{4})/g,
    (_: string, point: unknown, unit: unknown) =>
      typeof point === "string"
        ? String.fromCodePoint(parseInt(point, 16))
        : String.fromCharCode(
            parseInt(typeof unit === "string" ? unit : "", 16),
          ),
  );
}

export function quote(path: string): string {
  return path.replace(/[\\"]/g, (c) => `\\${c}`);
}

// Group 1 takes part in every match: a string.
export function doubled(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(/(\d)/g, (_: string, d: string) => d + d);
}

export function positions(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(
    /x/g,
    (m: string, at: number, input: string) => `${m}${at}/${input.length}`,
  );
}

export function named(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(
    /(?<word>\w+)|-/g,
    (
      m: string,
      word: string | undefined,
      at: number,
      input: string,
      groups: { readonly [k: string]: string | undefined },
    ) => groups["word"] ?? `${m}${at}${input.length}${word ?? ""}`,
  );
}

export function every(s: string): string {
  return s.replaceAll(/(a)/g, (_: string, a: string) => a.toUpperCase());
}

    let node = this.head;
    const log = this.log;
    return {
      next: (): IteratorResult<number> => {
        const current = node;
        if (current === null) return { done: true, value: undefined };
        node = current.next;
        return { done: false, value: current.value };
      },
      return: (): IteratorResult<number> => {
        log.closed = log.closed + 1;
        return { done: true, value: undefined };
      },
    };
  }
}

  if (a === undefined || c === undefined) return 0;
  return a + c;
}

  const [head, ...rest] = list;
  return head === undefined ? [] : rest;
}

  const [first] = values;
  return first ?? "";

  • declaration-list-order order agreement refused → verified pipeline verified: the pattern's bindings at the yielded values
    // A declaration list runs its declarators in order: the iterator steps and
// the close of the first declarator's pattern over an iterable the program
// defines, then the second declarator's initializer, which writes the same
// log, then a default reading the bindings of both. Under Node,
// `order(new Steps([]))` returns "next,return,second:s,s3".
class Steps {
  constructor(readonly log: string[]) {}
  [Symbol.iterator](): Iterator<string> {
    const log = this.log;
    return {
      next: (): IteratorResult<string> => {
        log.push("next");
        return { done: false, value: "s" };
      },
      return: (): IteratorResult<string> => {
        log.push("return");
        return { done: true, value: undefined };
      },
    };
  }
}

function note(
  log: string[],
  text: string,
): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, number> {
  log.push(text);
  return log.length;
}

export function order(steps: Steps): string {
  const log = steps.log;
  const [first] = steps,
    count = note(log, `second:${first ?? ""}`),
    [both = `${first ?? ""}${count}`] = [undefined];
  return `${log.join(",")},${both}`;
}

Copy a dictionary's indexes and a function's fields in a spread, as the producer's alternatives

no-behaviour-change

Why

A spread or Object.assign of a dictionary or of a function with fields was not handled ("a spread of a value of no record contract"): the walk's copy rule lacked the producer's index, symbol and numeric alternatives and its callable one.

modifiedProposal the walk: the copies a spread's operand gives

modifiedProposal the walk: merging a copy with an indexed side

Mirrors

ocaml-producer/object_spread.ml (alternatives_of, merge_alternative, alternative_type).

modifiedDocs single-pass.md, §9 "Classes"

States the copies.

Soundness

The single pass checks each copy at the allocation and at its use. No unit newly accepted where the pipeline refuses. invalid-spread-intersection-indexes, accepted by both modes under the copy's first version, stays not handled (two index signatures of one key class, the producer's restriction, mirrored). The three spread-intersection units both modes accept (invalid-spread-intersection-union-product, -disjoint-literals, -optional-narrowing copied) are unchanged: the pipeline refuses them at the producer's refusal.

export function onLiteral(): { a: number; b: boolean; c: string } {
  const o = { a: 1 };
  const before = o.a;
  o.b = before > 0;
  o["c"] = "s";
  return o;
}

// Added on one path only: where the paths join the key is optional, which
// the object's exact keys state.
export function inBranch(c: boolean): { x?: number } {
  const o = {};
  if (c) {
    o.x = 1;
  }
  return o;
}

// A declaration inside the loop body is a fresh object each time round.
export function inLoop(n: number): number {
  let total = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const o = {};
    o.v = i;
    total = total + o.v;
  }
  return total;
}

// An object a spread built is fresh too.
export function spreadBuilt(p: { a: number }): { a: number; b: string } {
  const o = { ...p };
  o.b = "b";
  return o;
}

// An optional field of the annotation, written: its key added at its type.
export function optionalAnnotated(): { a?: number; b: number } {
  const o: { a?: number; b: number } = { b: 0 };
  o.a = 3;
  return o;
}

// A `let` holding its own copy, and a constant bound to it since: the copy
// with the key is rebound to both, the cell and the constant.
export function inCellWithAlias(src: { [k: string]: number }): number {
  let o = { ...src };
  const ref = o;
  o.x = 5;
  return (ref.x ?? 0) + o.x;
}

// A `new` of a class the file declares: its constructor reads no `this` and
// ends in the instance's allocation, which nothing else has reached.
class WithOptional {
  x: number = 0;
  constructor(public y?: string) {}
}
export function onInstance(): string | undefined {
  const b = new WithOptional("s");
  b.y = undefined;
  return b.y;
}

// A write through an annotated constant bound to the object: every holder
// holds the copy with the key, at which a view stating the key reads it.
export function throughAnnotatedAlias(): number {
  const o = { y: 0 };
  const w: { x?: number; y: number } = o;
  w.x = 1;
  const view: { x?: number } = o;
  return (view.x ?? 0) + (w.x ?? 0);
}

  for (const x of s) {

  let total = 0;
  for (const entry of m) {
    const pair: [string, number] = entry;
    total += pair[1];
  }
  return total;
}

export function keysUntil(m: Map<string, number>, stop: string): string {
  let out = "";
  for (const k of m.keys()) {
    if (k === stop) break;
    out = out + k;
  }
  return out;
}

export function values(m: Map<string, boolean>): number {
  let n = 0;
  for (const v of m.values()) if (v) n = n + 1;
  return n;
}

export function setEntries(s: Set<number>): number {
  let total = 0;
  for (const e of s.entries()) total += e[0] + e[1];
  return total;
}

export function literal(): number {
  let n = 0;
  for (const c of "abc")
    for (const x of new Set<number>([1, 2])) n = n + x + c.length;
  return n;
}

    // The guard keeping the found fields with its parameter inferred: the
// producer claims the parameter at the arms of `TypeTerm | null`, and does
// not select `filter`'s guard signature, so the result is claimed at the
// element type with `null` and does not meet `union`'s `TypeTerm[]`.
// `blocker-last-indexed-access-fields` names the parameter's type.
// Census functions: computed-types.mts#indexedAccess.
import type { TypeTerm } from "../../tools/declaration-types.mts";

type ObjectTerm = Extract<TypeTerm, { k: "object" }>;

const union = (parts: TypeTerm[]): TypeTerm => {
  const [only] = parts;
  return parts.length === 1 && only ? only : { k: "union", parts, span: [0, 0] };
};

export function fields(object: ObjectTerm, keys: TypeTerm[]): TypeTerm | null {
  const parts = keys.map((key) => {
    if (key.k !== "literal" || key.name !== "string") return null;
    const field = object.fields.find((f) => f.name === key.text);
    return field ? field.type : null;
  });
  const found = parts.filter((p): p is TypeTerm => p !== null);
  return found.length === parts.length ? union(found) : null;
}

type State = { segments: number };
let state: State | null = null;

function count(): number {
  if (state === null) state = { segments: 0 };
  const s: State = state;
  s.segments++;
  return s.segments;
}

// old one; a local `let` a closure updates before its declaration is an
// early binding too.
let n: number = 1;
function reset(): number {
  n = 10;
  return 5;
}
export function compound(): number {
  n += reset();
  return n;
}

  calls++;
  return "v";

let s: string | null = null;
let t: string = "";
let u: boolean = true;
function test(): boolean {
  calls++;
  return false;
}
export function logical(): string {

  t ||= side();
  t ||= side();
  const second = t;
  u &&= test();
  u &&= test();
  return first + second + u + calls;
}

  return before * 100 + n;
}

    return ++k;
  };
  const dec = (): number => {
    return k--;
  };
  let k: number = 0;
  inc();
  inc();
  const was = dec();
  return was * 10 + k;
