    // `try`: a throw may come from any point of the body, so the handler and the
// finalizer start from the cells' contracts, not from what the body wrote;
// the caught value is `unknown`, and a `typeof` test narrows it. A `throw`
// leaves the function unless a `try` catches it; the `finally` block runs on
// every way out, a `return` included, which then resumes.
function recover(mayThrow: () => void): number {
  let y: number | null = 1;
  try {
    y = 2;
    mayThrow();
  } catch (e) {
    const caught: unknown = e;
    y = 0;
  }
  if (y === null) {
    return -1;
  }
  return y;
}

function cleanup(mayThrow: () => void): boolean {
  let done: boolean = false;
  try {
    mayThrow();
  } finally {
    done = true;
  }
  return done;
}

function both(mayThrow: () => void): number {
  let y: number = 0;
  try {
    mayThrow();
    y = 1;
  } catch {
    y = 2;
  } finally {
    y = y + 1;
  }
  return y;
}

function returnsFromHandler(mayThrow: () => number): number {
  try {
    return mayThrow();
  } catch (e: unknown) {
    return 0;
  }
}

function raise(x: number | null): number {
  if (x === null) {
    throw "no value";
  }
  return x;
}

function handled(x: number | null): number {
  try {
    if (x === null) {
      throw x;
    }
    return x;
  } catch {
    return 0;
  }
}

function describe(f: () => string): string {
  try {
    return f();
  } catch (e) {
    if (typeof e === "string") {
      return e;
    }
    return "unknown";
  }
}

function rethrow(f: () => number): number {
  try {
    return f();
  } catch (e) {
    throw e;
  }
}

function returnThroughFinally(
  f: () => number,
  log: (n: number) => void,
): number {
  let seen: number = 0;
  try {
    return f();
  } finally {
    log(seen);
  }
}

function nested(f: () => number, g: () => void): number {
  try {
    try {
      return f();
    } finally {
      g();
    }
  } catch {
    return -1;
  }
}

function finallyOverrides(f: () => number): number {
  try {
    return f();
  } finally {
    return 0;
  }
}

async function awaited(p: Promise<number>): Promise<number> {
  try {
    return await p;
  } catch {
    return 0;
  }
}

function links(f: () => number, o: { a: number }): number {
  let c: number = 0;
  try {
    c = f();
    o.a = c;
  } catch (e) {
    c = o.a;
  } finally {
    o.a = 1;
  }
  return c;
}

function loopTry(xs: number[], f: (n: number) => number): number {
  let total: number = 0;
  for (const x of xs) {
    try {
      total = total + f(x);
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
  }
  return total;
}

    // A `break` or `continue` leaving a `try` runs its `finally` on the way,
// innermost first, each in its `try`'s context, then lands; a `finally`
// that jumps itself leaves by its own way.
export function breakThroughFinally(xs: number[]): number {
  let count = 0;
  for (const x of xs) {
    try {
      if (x < 0) {
        break;
      }
      count = count + 1;
    } finally {
      count = count * 2;
    }
  }
  return count;
}

export function continueThroughTwo(xs: number[]): number {
  let n = 0;
  for (const x of xs) {
    try {
      try {
        if (x > 0) continue;
        n = n + 1;
      } finally {
        n = n + 2;
      }
    } finally {
      n = n + 3;
    }
  }
  return n;
}

export function switchThroughFinally(k: number): "a" | "b" {
  let x: "a" | "b" = "a";
  switch (k) {
    case 1:
      try {
        break;
      } finally {
        x = "b";
      }
    default:
      x = "a";
  }
  return x;
}

export function exitState(n: number): "b" {
  let x: "a" | "b" = "a";
  let i = 0;
  while (i < n) {
    i = i + 1;
    try {
      x = "a";
      break;
    } finally {
      x = "b";
    }
  }
  if (x === "a") return "b";
  return x;
}

export function jumpFromCatch(c: () => boolean, mayThrow: () => void): number {
  let n = 0;
  while (c()) {
    try {
      mayThrow();
    } catch {
      break;
    } finally {
      n = 1;
    }
  }
  return n;
}

export function finallyOverridesJump(c: () => boolean): number {
  while (c()) {
    try {
      break;
    } finally {
      return 1;
    }
  }
  return 0;

// instance or initialize a callable object are graph code as any other: a
// rest's store, a default and the parameters are bound at the code's entry,
// and loops, `switch`, `try` and mutable locals run inside.
function sumRest(seed: number): number {
  const sum = (first: number, ...rest: number[]): number => {
    let total = first;
    for (const x of rest) total += x;
    return total;
  };
  return sum(seed, 1, 2) + sum(seed);
}
function tupleRest(seed: number): number {
  const pick = (...pair: [number, string]): number => {
    let result = 0;
    switch (pair[1]) {
      case "a":
        result = pair[0];
        break;
      default:
        result = 1;
    }
    return result;
  };
  return pick(seed, "a");
}
function defaulted(seed: number): number {
  const scale = (x: number, by: number = 2): number => x * by;
  const later = (
    x: number,
    read: () => number = (): number => y,
    y: number = x,
  ): number => read();

}

    let n = 0;

    try {
      return fallback;

  return first(seed);

    // An `Iterable<number>` may be any object with a `[Symbol.iterator]`: the
// loop runs its iterator by the protocol, typed by the standard library's

export function first(values: Iterable<number>): number {
  for (const v of values) return v;

export function firstPositive(values: Iterable<number | null>): number {
  for (const v of values) {
    if (v !== null && v > 0) return v;
  }

export function wrong(vs: number[], log: number[]): number[] {

export function use(stop: boolean): { first(): number } {
  return {
    first: () => {
      while (true) {
        try {
          return 1;
        } finally {
          if (stop) break;

    // Census functions: fragment-expressions.mts#expr,#objectFields,#optionalChain,
// #optionalMethodCall,#wrappedMethodCall,#chainLink,#update,#template,#binary,#lambda.
import * as ts from "typescript/unstable/ast";
import type { Gate } from "../../tools/fragment-parse.mts";
export function receiver(
  this: Gate,
  node: ts.Expression,
): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, number> {
  const gate: Gate = this;
  if (ts.isCallExpression(node)) {
    if (
      ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(node.expression) &&
      node.expression.name.text === "apply" &&
      gate.libraryName(node.expression.name)
    ) {
      return 0;
    }
    if (
      ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(node.expression) &&
      ["call", "bind"].includes(node.expression.name.text) &&
      gate.libraryName(node.expression.name)
    ) {
      if (
        node.questionDotToken ||
        node.expression.questionDotToken ||
        node.typeArguments?.length ||
        node.arguments.length === 0 ||
        node.arguments.some((arg) => ts.isSpreadElement(arg)) ||
        !gate.knownLocal(node.expression.expression)
      )
        gate.refuseReceiverForm(node, "receiver");
      return node.arguments.length;
    }
  }
  return 0;
}

Admit omitted undefined arguments and saved tuple spreads in constructions

no-behaviour-change

Why

Boolean's value parameter admits undefined, so filter(Boolean) and Boolean() may omit it, but the walk's test of which signatures fit a call counts only optional parameters as omissible and found no signature (library-boolean-value truthy@599). A construction whose tuple spread is followed by effectful actuals has a lowering that saves the operands first, while the walk applied the ordinary call's restriction to it (constructor-tuple-spread snapshot@401).

modifiedProposal the walk: a construction with a tuple spread

Soundness

Operand evaluation and the snapshot's construction stay the existing lowering's checks; the call's step checks each actual at the chosen signature.

    class Pair {
  first: number;
  second: string;
  constructor(first: number, second: string) {
    this.first = first;
    this.second = second;
  }
}
class Box<T> {
  value: T;
  constructor(value: T) {
    this.value = value;
  }
}
function replace(xs: [number]): string {
  xs[0] = 2;
  return "changed";
}
function choose(xs: [number]): typeof Pair {
  xs[0] = 1;
  return Pair;
}
export function snapshot(): number {
  const xs: [number] = [0];
  const result = new (choose(xs))(...xs, replace(xs));
  return result.first * 10 + xs[0];
}
export function multiple(): number {
  const first: readonly [number] = [3];
  const second: [string] = ["ok"];
  return new Pair(...first, ...second).first;
}
export function generic(): string {
  const args: [string] = ["ok"];
  return new Box(...args).value;
}
export function explicit(): number {
  const args: [number] = [4];
  return new Box<number>(...args).value;
}
export function empty(): number {
  const args: [] = [];
  return new Pair(...args, 5, "ok").first;
}

    // `Boolean` read as a value, the callable `(value: unknown) => boolean`:
// passed to `filter`, `every` and `some`, which call it with an element, an
// index and the array, of which it converts the first alone; held in a
// constant and called; and called directly, of no argument too.
export function words(line: string): string[] {
  return line.split(" ").filter(Boolean);
}

export function allSet(flags: readonly boolean[]): boolean {
  return flags.every(Boolean);
}

export function anyObject(values: readonly (object | null)[]): boolean {
  return values.some(Boolean);
}

export function truthy(v: unknown): boolean {
  const test: (value: unknown) => boolean = Boolean;
  return test(v) && Boolean(v) && !Boolean();
}

a recursive constant's self reads.

Effect

  • recursive-constant-callback anyBinder agreement disagreed → verified pipeline verified: a self read offers the longer signature
    // A recursive constant passing its own name as a callback in its body: the
// read is the closure's self entry, which holds the closure at its whole
// claim, so the closure is offered the callback's longer signature there as
// where any other read passes it, and its code is checked at that signature
// with the self entry at the claim. Module-level and local, annotated
// directly and through an alias, in a nested callback after a union test,
// bound under an annotation of a longer signature that a later call passes
// more arguments, read by a default and through a bound wrapper, and at a
// variadic signature whose fixed parameters cover the closure's.
type Term =
  | { readonly k: "binder"; readonly name: string }
  | { readonly k: "union"; readonly parts: readonly Term[] }
  | { readonly k: "atom"; readonly name: string };

const binder = (t: Term): boolean =>
  t.k === "binder" || (t.k === "union" && t.parts.some(binder));

export function hasBinder(t: Term): boolean {
  return binder(t);
}

export function anyBinder(terms: readonly Term[]): boolean {
  return terms.some((part) => {
    if (part.k !== "union") return false;
    const local = (t: Term): boolean =>
      t.k === "binder" || (t.k === "union" && t.parts.every(local));
    return local(part);
  });
}

export function annotated(t: Term): boolean {
  const open: (t: Term) => boolean = (u) =>
    u.k !== "union" || u.parts.some(open);
  return open(t);
}

type Test = (t: Term) => boolean;

export function aliased(t: Term): boolean {
  const open: Test = (u) => u.k !== "union" || u.parts.every(open);
  return open(t);
}

type Step = (t: Term, depth: number) => string;

export function escaped(t: Term): string {
  const show = (u: Term): string => {
    const later: Step = show;
    if (u.k !== "union") return u.k;
    let out = "";
    for (const part of u.parts) out += later(part, 1);
    return out;
  };
  return show(t);
}

type Row = (n: number, d: number | undefined, extra: string) => number;

export function defaultsAndBind(): number {
  const f = (n: number, d: number = n > 0 ? f(0) : 0): number => {
    const again: Row = f;
    return n <= 0 ? d : again(n - 1, undefined, "ignored");
  };
  const bound = f.bind(null, 2);
  return bound();
}

type Rest = (n: number, ...extra: string[]) => number;

export function variadic(): number {
  const f = (n: number): number => {
    const again: Rest = f;
    return n <= 0 ? 0 : again(n - 1, "ignored", "also ignored");
  };
  return f(2);
}

  const show = (u: Term): string => {
    const later: Step = show;
    if (u.k !== "union") return u.k;
    let out = "";
    for (const part of u.parts) out += later(part, 1);
    return out;
  };
  return show(t);
}

type Row = (n: number, d: number | undefined, extra: string) => number;

export function defaultsAndBind(): number {
  const f = (n: number, d: number = n > 0 ? f(0) : 0): number => {
    const again: Row = f;
    return n <= 0 ? d : again(n - 1, undefined, "ignored");
  };
  const bound = f.bind(null, 2);
  return bound();
}

type Rest = (n: number, ...extra: string[]) => number;

export function variadic(): number {
  const f = (n: number): number => {
    const again: Rest = f;
    return n <= 0 ? 0 : again(n - 1, "ignored", "also ignored");
  };
  return f(2);
}

    // A closure over `Node` passed to a node list of `Expression`s: the
// callback's signature at the element is offered to it, since each
// expression is a node (SOURCE-ELABORATION.md, "Source closures and their
// annotations"). `Expression`'s arms are `Node`'s, its residual within
// `Node`'s by width and depth: a narrower tag, the members `Node`'s
// residual keeps, and a brand `Node`'s lacks. A recursive one, as
// `assignedNames`' `targets`, is offered it through its self entry.
import * as ts from "typescript/unstable/ast";

export function count(root: ts.ArrayLiteralExpression): number {
  let n = 0;
  const one = (e: ts.Node): void => {
    if (ts.isIdentifier(e)) n = n + 1;
  };
  root.elements.forEach(one);
  return n;
}

export function names(root: ts.Node): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const targets = (e: ts.Node): void => {
    if (ts.isIdentifier(e)) out.push(e.text);
    else if (ts.isArrayLiteralExpression(e)) e.elements.forEach(targets);
  };
  targets(root);
  return out;
}

    // A condition's tests refine where they run, and a later step acts on what
// they found: a call in the right operand of `&&` may write the field the
// left operand tested, so past it nothing is known of the field's contents,
// while the union arm the test selected stays a lifetime fact. A write of
// a local past its test leaves the local what was written.
type T =
  | { k: "atom"; name: string }
  | { k: "union" | "intersection"; parts: T[] };

export function parameterCall(operand: T, fail: (m: string) => never, binder: (t: T) => boolean): void {
  if (operand.k === "union" && binder(operand)) fail("a union holding a binder");
}

export function localCall(operand: T, fail: (m: string) => never): void {
  const binder = (t: T): boolean => t.k === "union" && t.parts.some(binder);
  if (operand.k === "union" && binder(operand)) fail("a union holding a binder");
  if (operand.k !== "union" || binder(operand)) return;
  fail("a union without a binder");
}

export function reassigned(x: string | number): boolean {
  return typeof x === "string" && (x = 0, x === 0);
}

    // An optional call through a `let` the loop assigns: the receiver is
// `undefined` on the first iteration and an array afterwards. A pass that
// finds the receiver only nullish claims the call's body at no value, being
// unreached; the loop's settled pass claims it at the array.
export function collect(lines: string[], into: string[]): number {
  let target: string[] | undefined;
  for (const line of lines) {
    target?.push(line);
    target = into;
  }
  return into.length;
}

// A receiver only `undefined` where the call runs: the body is never
// reached.
export function unreached(into: string[]): number {
  let target: string[] | undefined;
  target?.push("x");
  target = into;
  return target.length;
}

    // The standard library's `Float64Array` as pretext uses it
// (chenglou/pretext at 0d102a5c, src/measurement.ts): a record field that
// is a table or `null` or not computed yet, `new Float64Array(n).fill(NaN)`,
// an element read at a number, a table entry not asked yet being `NaN`, and
// an element write. A view's elements are any doubles, `NaN` included.
export type Measurement = {
  kanaKerning: Float64Array | null | undefined;
  size: number;
};

export function getKerning(
  measurement: Measurement,
  count: number,
): Float64Array | null {
  if (measurement.kanaKerning === undefined) {
    measurement.kanaKerning = null;
    if (count > 0)
      measurement.kanaKerning = new Float64Array(count * count).fill(NaN);
  }
  return measurement.kanaKerning;
}

export function kerningAt(
  kernings: Float64Array,
  index: number,
  measured: number,
): number {
  const kerning = kernings[index] ?? 0;
  return Number.isNaN(kerning) ? (kernings[index] = measured) : kerning;
}

export function total(kernings: Float64Array): number {
  let sum = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < kernings.length; i++) sum += kernings[i] ?? 0;
  return sum + new Float64Array([0.5, 0.25]).subarray(1).length;
}

no-behaviour-change

Why

An evolving let (declared nullish, later assigned) or an empty array needs the types of later writes at its declaration, where its store is allocated; a fresh array's first typed whole-value use can require a tuple or a wider element contract than its literal gives. The walk allocated each store at its initializer's type, and the units listed below disagreed with the pipeline at those proposals.

type List<T> = null | { head: T; tail: List<T> };

function reverse<T>(l: List<T>): List<T> {
  let result: List<T> = null;
  while (l !== null) {
    result = { head: l.head, tail: result };
    l = l.tail;
  }
  return result;
}

export function fromArray<T>(...elts: T[]): List<T> {
  let result = null;
  for (let i = 0; i < elts.length; i++) {
    const elt = elts[i];
    if (elt !== undefined) {
      result = { head: elt, tail: result };
    }
  }
  return reverse(result);
}

    // The iterator protocol over a union of iterables: GetIterator gives a union
// of iterators, and `next` (and `return`) is bound to whichever the iterator
// is, `%iterator.next.bind(%iterator)`, a member bound to a union of hosts.
// The bound function takes what every host's member takes and returns the
// union of their results: two `IteratorResult`s, each with its own
// `TReturn`, of which the loop reads the not-done arms' values.
class Countdown {
  left: number;
  constructor(left: number) {
    this.left = left;
  }
  next(): IteratorResult<number, undefined> {
    const n = this.left;
    if (n <= 0) return { done: true, value: undefined };
    this.left = n - 1;
    return { done: false, value: n };
  }
  return(): IteratorResult<number, undefined> {
    this.left = 0;
    return { done: true, value: undefined };
  }
  [Symbol.iterator](): Countdown {
    return this;
  }
}

// An iterator whose return value is a string: its `done` result's value.
class Repeat {
  times: number;
  readonly value: number;
  constructor(times: number, value: number) {
    this.times = times;
    this.value = value;
  }
  next(): IteratorResult<number, string> {
    const t = this.times;
    if (t <= 0) return { done: true, value: "finished" };
    this.times = t - 1;
    return { done: false, value: this.value };
  }
  return(): IteratorResult<number, string> {
    this.times = 0;
    return { done: true, value: "closed" };
  }
  [Symbol.iterator](): Repeat {
    return this;
  }
}

type Steps = Countdown | Repeat;

// The protocol over a union of iterables: `next` and `return` each bound to
// whichever iterator GetIterator gave; the values are the yields' `number`.
export function total(it: Steps): number {
  let sum = 0;
  for (const v of it) sum = sum + v;
  return sum;
}

// `break` closes the iterator through its `return`, bound the same way.
export function firstOver(it: Countdown | Repeat, limit: number): number {
  let found = -1;
  for (const v of it) {
    if (v > limit) {
      found = v;
      break;
    }
  }
  return found;
}

// The protocol in a closure's body.
export function later(it: Steps): () => number {
  return (): number => {
    let sum = 0;
    for (const v of it) sum = sum + v;
    return sum;
  };
}

// A union of a set and a readonly set: the spread runs the protocol over a
// `SetIterator` or the overlay's `Iterator`, its `next` bound to whichever.
export function merged(
  bound: ReadonlySet<string> | Set<string>,
  more: readonly string[],
): number {
  return new Set([...bound, ...more]).size;
}

// An alias nested in a union: the host's labels, not the spelling, split.
export function nestedAlias(it: Steps | Countdown): number {
  let sum = 0;
  for (const v of it) sum = sum + v;
  return sum;
}

// One host: its member bound to it, returning its own result.
export function countdown(it: Countdown): number {
  let sum = 0;
  for (const v of it) sum = sum + v;
  return sum;
}

    this.left = n - 1;
    return { done: false, value: n };
  }
  return(): IteratorResult<number, undefined> {
    return { done: true, value: undefined };
  }
  [Symbol.iterator](): Countdown {
    return this;
  }
}

class Bare {
  next(): number {
    return 1;
  }
  return(): IteratorResult<number, undefined> {
    return { done: true, value: undefined };
  }
  [Symbol.iterator](): Bare {
    return this;
  }
}

export function first(it: Countdown | Bare): number {
  for (const v of it) return v;
  return 0;
}

// the arm holding only `null`: the cell may be of that arm, so the write's
// obligation fails, though TypeScript admits it.

type Cell = { value: null | boolean } | { value: null };

function writeTrue(): null | boolean {
  const cell: Cell = { value: null };

// type-term.mts's `members` builds a class value's static fields. Arrays are
// invariant, so the result at the callback's own record types would not meet
// that field's contract.
type Field = { name: string; type: number; readonly?: true };
type Term =
  | { k: "constructor"; arity: number; statics?: Field[] }
  | { k: "atom"; name: string };

export function statics(
  only: { k: "constructor"; arity: number },
  fields: { name: string; type: number; readonly: boolean }[],
): Term {
  const statics = fields.map((f) => ({
    name: f.name,
    type: f.type,
    ...(f.readonly ? { readonly: true as const } : {}),
  }));
  return { ...only, statics };
}

    // A closure reading a `let` declared after it, the `let` unannotated and
// initialized by a literal: the binding is early, and its stated type is
// the literal's primitive type, TypeScript's declared type for it. Census
// functions: fragment-statements.mts#markEarly (`let statementStart = -1`
// read in `visit`) and the functions whose slices include it, functionDecl,
// protocolPattern, switchStmt, controlStmt and hoistTarget among them.
export function starts(lengths: readonly number[]): number[] {
  const out: number[] = [];
  const visit = (n: number): void => {
    out.push(start + n);
  };
  let start = -1;
  for (const n of lengths) {
    start = n;
    visit(n);
  }
  return out;
}

// A `let` nothing assigns, read through the earlier closure.
export function unassigned(): number {
  const read = (): number => x;
  let x = -1;
  return read();
}

// The other primitive families: a string, a Boolean and a bigint.
export function families(): string {
  const label = (): string => `${name}:${on}:${big}`;
  let name = "a";
  let on = true;
  let big = -2n;
  name = name + "b";
  on = !on;
  big = big * 3n;
  return label();
}

// The closure run before the declaration: the read throws a ReferenceError.
export function tooEarly(): number {
  const read = (): number => x;
  const value = read();
  let x = 1;
  return value + x;
}
  • module-cache-before-initialization rhs@341 agreement refused → verified pipeline verified: the same declaration rule
    // A module's own cache written before its declaration runs: the write reads
// the cache's binding first, as JavaScript does, so the ReferenceError comes
// before the right side runs (`before` is 0); after the declaration the
// write adds the key (`after` is 1). Run under Node.
type Table = "a" | "b";
let effects: number = 0;

function rhs(): number[] {
  effects = effects + 1;
  return [effects];
}

function fill(table: Table): number[] {
  return (cache[table] = rhs());
}

function attempt(): number {
  try {
    fill("a");
  } catch {
    return effects;
  }
  return -1;
}

export const before: number = attempt();
const cache: Partial<Record<Table, number[]>> = {};
export const after: number = fill("b").length;

with Claude Fable 5.2
67c3b5757 · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 11, 19:21

Call a member at the signatures of the walked receiver

no-behaviour-change

Why

An array's methods state their signatures at two receivers, a dense array and a sparse one. For mapped.filter((value) => value > 0), mapped a sparse map result, the walk walked the callback at the first signature's parameter, the dense receiver's, and stated the member at every signature: the callback's third parameter was the dense array, no signature of the sparse receiver admitted it, and the receiver's obligation was read off the dense signature. The producer reads the member at the walked receiver and claims the selected signature.

modifiedProposal the walk: a method call's candidate signatures

Soundness

The signatures stated are the member's own declared signatures; the pass derives the call from them, the receiver's obligation included (the pass's direct call, lean/Verification/Programs/SinglePass.lean:611), and checks each callback's body at the signature it is stated at.

    // A `map` callback whose only program call is one typed `never` at its
// instance: the call never returns normally, so on normal return it changes
// nothing, the callback is within the empty footprint and the result is
// dense. The call is a class member's, a generic function's instance at
// `never`, and a function's with a rest parameter, none of whose signatures
// states an effect a `map` callback could use.
export class Gate {
  prefix: string = "";
  fail(message: string): never {
    throw new Error(this.prefix + message);
  }
}

export function members(gate: Gate, xs: string[]): string[] {
  const r: string[] = xs.map((x) => {
    if (x === "") return gate.fail("empty");
    return x;
  });
  return r;
}

function die<T>(message: string): T {
  throw new Error(message);
}

export function instances(xs: number[]): number[] {
  const r: number[] = xs.map((x) => {
    if (x < 0) return die<never>("negative");
    return x;
  });
  return r;
}

function failAll(...parts: string[]): never {
  throw new Error(parts.join(" "));
}

export function rests(xs: string[]): string[] {
  const r: string[] = xs.map((x) => {
    if (x === "") return failAll("empty", "string");
    return x;
  });
  return r;
}

// An async function and an async arrow whose bodies reach no completion: a
// call of the never-returning `stop`, then a throw. An async call returns
// its promise where its body throws, so each verifies at the footprint
// letting every location change, as every async definition does.
export async function rejected(
  xs: number[],
  stop: (xs: number[]) => never,
): Promise<number> {
  stop(xs);
  throw new Error("unreached");
}

export function rejecting(): (
  xs: number[],
  stop: (xs: number[]) => never,
) => Promise<number> {
  return async (
    ys: number[],
    stop: (ys: number[]) => never,
  ): Promise<number> => {
    stop(ys);
    throw new Error("unreached");
  };
}

// An async recursive constant whose body reaches no completion: it calls
// itself, then the never-returning `stop`, then throws. It verifies at the
// footprint letting every location change.
export const countdown = async (
  n: number,
  stop: (n: number) => never,
): Promise<number> => {
  if (n > 0) countdown(n - 1, stop);
  stop(n);
  throw new Error("unreached");
};

import * as ts from "typescript/unstable/ast";
import type {
  TypeAliasDeclaration,
  TypeReferenceNode,
  TypeParameterDeclaration,
} from "typescript/unstable/ast";
import type { TermScope } from "../../tools/type-term.mts";
import type { TypeTerm } from "../../tools/declaration-types.mts";
export function extend(
  scope: TermScope,
  alias: TypeAliasDeclaration,
  parameters: readonly TypeParameterDeclaration[],
  inputs: readonly TypeTerm[],
  expandingAliases: Set<TypeAliasDeclaration>,
): TermScope {
  const inner: TermScope = {
    ...scope,
    source: alias.getSourceFile(),
    expandingAliases,
    awaited: (reference) => {
      const name = reference.typeName;
      return (
        !(
          ts.isIdentifier(name) &&
          parameters.some((p) => p.name.text === name.text)
        ) &&
        (scope.awaited?.(reference) ?? false)
      );
    },
    associatedAlias: (reference) => {
      const name = reference.typeName;
      return ts.isIdentifier(name) &&
        parameters.some((p) => p.name.text === name.text)
        ? null
        : (scope.associatedAlias?.(reference) ?? null);
    },
    named(reference, position, read) {
      const name = reference.typeName;
      const index = ts.isIdentifier(name)
        ? parameters.findIndex((p) => p.name.text === name.text)
        : -1;
      if (index < 0) return scope.named(reference, position, read);
      const input = inputs[index];
      if (!input || reference.typeArguments?.length)
        return scope.fail(reference, "invalid alias argument");
      return input;
    },
  };
  return inner;
}

/*
 * Receivers. The directive above makes this code strict, which is the receiver
 * rule the verifier models: a call passes its receiver unchanged, and a plain
 * call passes `undefined`. Each function returns what a reader can predict from
 * the receiver it names; tests/methods.mts runs them and checks each against
 * the value the wrong receiver would give.

/** A property call passes its object, parenthesized or not; a copied method
 * is a value, and a plain call of it passes `undefined`. */
function propertyCall(seed: boolean): boolean {
  const owner = {
    value: seed,
    get(this: { value: boolean }): boolean {
      return this.value;
    },
    constant(): boolean {
      return true;
    },
  };
  const copied = owner.constant;
  const direct = owner.get();
  // The parentheses are the point: a formatter would drop them.
  // prettier-ignore
  const grouped = (owner.get)();
  const constant = copied();
  return constant ? (direct ? grouped : !grouped) : false;
}

/** `.call` rebinds an ordinary function. The arrow it returns keeps the
 * receiver of the call that created it: `this` in an arrow is a capture. */
function callRebinds(seed: boolean): boolean {
  const first = { value: seed };
  const second = { value: !seed };
  const reader = function (this: { value: boolean }): () => boolean {
    return (): boolean => this.value;
  };
  const kept = reader.call(first);
  const rebound = reader.call(second);
  return kept() ? !rebound() : rebound();
}

/** The method is read and saved before the actuals run: an actual that
 * replaces the field changes the next call, not this one. */

  const owner: {
    value: boolean;
    pick: (this: { value: boolean }, x: boolean) => boolean;
  } = {
    value: seed,

      return this.value;
    },
  };

    return !this.value;
  };
  const replace = (): boolean => {
    owner.pick = flip;
    return true;
  };
  const first = owner.pick(replace());
  const second = owner.pick(true);

// (type-probe.mts, its `marked`).
interface Item {
  kind: "named" | "plain";
  pos: number;
}
interface Named extends Item {
  kind: "named";
  name: string;
}
interface Plain extends Item {
  kind: "plain";
}
type Entry = Named | Plain;

export function boxed(box: { value: number }): number {
  const read = <T>(b: { value: T }): T => b.value;
  return read(box);
}

export function among(items: readonly Named[], at: number): string {
  const resolvedAmong = <T extends Item>(
    candidates: readonly T[],
  ): T | undefined => candidates.find((m) => m.pos === at);
  const found = resolvedAmong(items);
  return found ? found.name : "";
}

export function marked(entry: Entry): string {
  const select = <N extends Entry>(
    test: (n: Entry) => n is N,
  ): N | undefined => (test(entry) ? entry : undefined);
  const found = select((n: Entry): n is Named => n.kind === "named");
  return found ? found.name : "";
}

    // A module's own cache written before its declaration runs: the write reads
// the cache's binding first, as JavaScript does, so the ReferenceError comes
// before the right side runs (`before` is 0); after the declaration the
// write adds the key (`after` is 1). Run under Node.
type Table = "a" | "b";
let effects: number = 0;

function rhs(): number[] {
  effects = effects + 1;
  return [effects];
}

function fill(table: Table): number[] {
  return (cache[table] = rhs());
}

function attempt(): number {
  try {
    fill("a");
  } catch {
    return effects;
  }
  return -1;
}

export const before: number = attempt();
const cache: Partial<Record<Table, number[]>> = {};
export const after: number = fill("b").length;

/** A cell allocated by each iteration, written: the parameter's field keeps its test. */
export function loopCells(x: { value: number | null }, n: number): number {
  let total = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (x.value === null) return total;
    let count = 0;
    const read = (): number => count;
    const v = (count = x.value);
    total = total + x.value + v + read();
  }
  return total;

  if (x.value === null) return 0;
  let c = b ? 1 : 2;
  const read = (): number => c;
  const v = (c = x.value);
  return x.value + v + read();

  let c = 1;

  try {

export function aside<T>(run: () => T): T {

  retained = null;

  } finally {

export function count(xs: number[]): number {
  let found = 0;
  const visit = (x: number): void => {
    if (wanted(x)) found++;
  };
  const wanted = (x: number): boolean => x > 10;
  for (const x of xs) visit(x);
  return found;
}

// An early `let`, assigned after its declaration: the closure reads its
// current contents.
export function later(): number {
  const get = (): number => n;
  let n: number = 1;
  n = 2;
  return get();
}

// A call before the declaration runs: the checked access throws there.
export function tooSoon(): number {
  const get = (): number => n;
  const x = get();
  const n: number = 1;
  return x + n;
}

// A block entered once per iteration: each entry has its own binding.
export function perIteration(xs: number[]): number {
  let total = 0;
  for (const x of xs) {
    const add = (): number => y;
    const y: number = x;
    total += add();
  }
  return total;
}

// `typeof` of an early binding is a checked access too.
export function kind(): boolean {
  const test = (): boolean => typeof v === "number";
  const v: number = 1;
  return test();
}

// An early binding holding an object, read in closure term code: its
// checked access may find either, and calls the intrinsic at its own type.
export function boxed(): number {
  const get = (): number => box.n;
  const box: { n: number } = { n: 1 };
  return get();
}

    // An unannotated constant holding a `map` result is built at the array type
// its first use expects: here a field of a returned object literal, as
// type-term.mts's `members` builds a class value's static fields. Arrays are
// invariant, so the result at the callback's own record types would not meet
// that field's contract.
type Field = { name: string; type: number; readonly?: true };
type Term =
  | { k: "constructor"; arity: number; statics?: Field[] }
  | { k: "atom"; name: string };

export function statics(
  only: { k: "constructor"; arity: number },
  fields: { name: string; type: number; readonly: boolean }[],
): Term {
  const statics = fields.map((f) => ({
    name: f.name,
    type: f.type,
    ...(f.readonly ? { readonly: true as const } : {}),
  }));
  return { ...only, statics };
}
  • object-spread-exact-literals params@488 agreement refused → verified pipeline verified: a const assertion's literal kept
    // An object literal a closure without a result annotation returns, and a
// constant's literal a later spread copies, own exactly the keys they write:
// the copy keeps every key written before it that the spread's literals
// lack (SOURCE-MODEL.md, "Object literals").
type P = { name: string; type: number; dots: boolean };

// A closure's literals, spread, then mapped at TypeScript's inferred union
// `{ name, type, rest: true } | { name, type, rest?: undefined }`.
export function params(ps: P[]): [string, number][] {
  const rest = (p: P) => (p.dots ? { rest: true as const } : {});
  const all = ps.map((p, i) => {
    if (p.dots) return { name: p.name, type: p.type, ...rest(p) };
    return { name: "x" + i, type: 0 };
  });
  return all.map((q): [string, number] => [q.name, q.type]);
}

// A constant's literals, spread.
export function local(p: P): string {
  const extra = p.dots ? { rest: true as const } : {};
  const o = { name: p.name, ...extra };
  return o.name;
}

// A key two spreads may give: the later one's where it holds it.
export function twice(p: P): number | string {
  const a = () => ({ k: 1 });
  const b = () => (p.dots ? { k: "s" } : {});
  const o = { ...a(), ...b() };
  return o.k;
}

// A key a spread may give, then written: the written one's.
export function later(p: P): string {
  const o = { ...(p.dots ? { name: 1 } : {}), name: "x" };
  return o.name;
}

// An async closure's literals: the payload its promise resolves with.
export async function awaited(p: P): Promise<string> {
  const rest = async () => (p.dots ? { rest: true as const } : {});
  const o = { name: p.name, ...(await rest()) };
  return o.name;
}

// A literal a writable dictionary is expected at is allocated at it: no
// own-key bound meets a writable index.
export function dictionary(): Record<string, number> {
  const make: () => Record<string, number> = () => ({ a: 1 });
  return make();
}

// loop runs its iterator by the protocol, typed by the standard library's
// `Iterable`, `Iterator` and `IteratorResult`. Left early by `return`, it
// calls the iterator's `return` where it has one, after the returned value
// is read.
export function first(values: Iterable<number>): number {
  for (const v of values) return v;
  return 0;
}

// A guard on the loop's element holds for the element it tested.
export function firstPositive(values: Iterable<number | null>): number {

    if (v !== null && v > 0) return v;

  return 0;
}

    // An entry that states signatures as a value or a function, or as a list:
// the absence of both is tested by nested tests, and the printed list is
// kept where every signature has a spelling, by a filter of the spelled ones
// and a length comparison. Stands for the census function
// shadow-contracts.mts#statedSignatures and its dependent #shadowText.
type Stated = { params: string[] };
type Entry = {
  global: string;
  stated?: Stated | ((n: number) => Stated);
  forms?: Stated[];
};

const print = (s: Stated): string | null =>
  s.params.length ? s.params.join(", ") : null;

export function signatures(entry: Entry): string[] | null | undefined {
  if (entry.stated === undefined) {
    if (entry.forms === undefined) return undefined;
  }
  const n = 1;
  const stated =
    typeof entry.stated === "function" ? entry.stated(n) : entry.stated;
  const printed = [
    ...(stated === undefined ? [] : [stated]),
    ...(entry.forms ?? []),
  ].map(print);
  const spelled = printed.filter((p): p is string => p !== null);
  return spelled.length === printed.length ? spelled : null;
}

    // A binder bounded by another is the meet of the two parameter rows, within
// the other's bound when it has one: below the other binder, and below its
// bound.
class DependentBox<T, U extends T> {
  first: T;
  second: U;
  constructor(first: T, second: U) {
    this.first = first;
    this.second = second;
  }
}

function widen<T extends string | number, U extends T>(x: U): T {
  const y: T = x;
  return y;
}

function throughBound<T extends { size: number }, U extends T>(x: U): number {
  return x.size;
}

export function use(n: number): number {
  const box = new DependentBox(n, n);
  return box.second + widen<number, number>(n) + throughBound({ size: n });
}

Validation

import type { OverlayEntry } from "../../tools/array-prototype.mts";
export function entries(
  name: string,
  overlay: readonly OverlayEntry[],
  primitive: Readonly<
    Record<"string" | "number" | "boolean", readonly OverlayEntry[]>

    // A field of an immutable binding's object holds what was last written to
// it until a call or another write: `x.f = v` and `x.f ??= v` leave the
// field at the written value's nullish exclusions, and a strict test of a
// path of two members refines its witness (HOST-FAMILIES.md, "Entries"), as
// type-term.mts's `quantified` caches a binder's resolution slots and reads
// their result.
type Slots = { observation: string; result: string | null };
type Binder = { name: string; resolution: Slots | null };

function slots(name: string, resolvable: boolean): Slots {
  return {
    observation: `#observe:${name}`,
    result: resolvable ? `#resolve:${name}` : null,
  };
}

// The cached slots' result, where the binder's resolution is resolvable.
export function resolved(binder: Binder, resolvable: boolean): string | null {
  binder.resolution ??= slots(binder.name, resolvable);
  if (binder.resolution.result === null) return null;
  return binder.resolution.result;
}

// A plain write, then a read of the field it wrote.
export function written(binder: Binder): Slots {
  binder.resolution = slots(binder.name, false);
  return binder.resolution;
}

// A path of two members tested against `null` in one statement and read in
// the next.
export function result(binder: { readonly resolution: Slots }): string {
  if (binder.resolution.result === null) return "";
  return binder.resolution.result;
}

// A method of a scope whose type states its effect, writing a field of a
// binder it finds, an intersection whose principal operand states the field:
// a named field's write changes a value's location, within the statement's
// footprint, as `quantified`'s `associated` does.
type Scope = {
  associated: (name: string) => Modifies<{ values: "any" }, string | null>;
};

export function scope(binders: (Binder & { span: number })[]): Scope {
  return {
    associated(name) {
      const binder = binders.find((b) => b.name === name);
      if (!binder) return null;
      binder.resolution ??= slots(binder.name, true);
      return binder.resolution.result;
    },
  };
}

  const deep = (t: Tree, d: number): boolean =>
    d <= 0 || t.children.some((c) => deep(c, d - 1));
  return list.findIndex((t) => deep(t, depth));
}

export function firstAnnotated(list: readonly Tree[]): Tree | undefined {
  const open: (t: Tree) => boolean = (t) =>
    !t.leaf && t.children.every((c) => open(c));
  return list.find((t) => open(t));
}

    // A named closure whose parameter is wider than the element of the array it
// is passed to, here a union of which the element is one arm: it is offered
// the callback's longer signature at the element, and Lean checks its body
// there, the element within the closure's parameter.
type F = { k: "f"; n: number };
type A = { k: "a"; s: string };
type T = A | F;

export function visit(t: T): number {
  return t.k === "f" ? t.n : t.s.length;
}

export function each(calls: F[]): number {
  let total = 0;
  const go = (part: T): void => {
    total += visit(part);
  };
  calls.forEach(go);
  return total;
}

export function mapped(calls: F[]): string[] {
  const name = (t: T): string => t.k;
  return calls.map(name);
}

export function tested(calls: readonly F[]): boolean {
  const small = (t: T): boolean => visit(t) < 10;
  return calls.every(small) && calls.some(small);
}

// The element written inline, the parameter a written union of aliases.
export function inline(calls: { k: "f"; n: number }[]): number {
  let total = 0;
  const go = (part: A | F): void => {
    total += visit(part);
  };
  calls.forEach(go);
  return total;
}

// The element an alias of the union's arm, the parameter wider still.
type G = F;
export function widest(calls: G[]): string[] {
  const show = (v: T | null): string => (v === null ? "" : v.k);
  return calls.map(show);
}

// The closure changing storage: a captured array it pushes onto, and the
// mapped array itself, whose result is read with its holes.
export function collected(calls: F[]): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const add = (t: T): void => {
    out.push(t.k);
  };
  calls.forEach(add);
  return out;
}

export function shrinking(calls: F[]): (string | undefined)[] {
  const name = (t: T): string => {
    calls.pop();
    return t.k;
  };
  return calls.map(name);
}

// A guard closure wider than the element: `filter`'s guard overload.
export function present(calls: (F | null)[]): F[] {
  const isF = (t: T | null): t is F => t !== null && t.k === "f";
  return calls.filter(isF);
}

    // pretext measurement.ts: addMetrics counts each measurement in a module
// cache's field (`measurement.state.segments++`) and reads a module `let`
// binding. Reading a module binding changes no location, and a field
// update writes one location holding a number, so the function keeps every
// store (`{value: any, store: keep}`) and a caller's loop keeps the length
// its reads are bounded by.

type State = { segments: number };
let state: State | null = null;

function count(): number {
  if (state === null) state = { segments: 0 };
  const s: State = state;
  s.segments++;
  return s.segments;
}

export function total(xs: number[]): number {
  let t = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; i++) t += count() + xs[i]!;
  return t;
}

type Profile = { epsilon: number };

let cached: Profile | null = null;

function build(): Profile {
  return { epsilon: 0.005 };
}

export function getProfile(): Profile {
  return cached ??= build();
}

export function reset(): void {
  cached = null;
}

/** @invariant this.segmentFlags.length === this.widths.length */
export type Prepared = { widths: number[]; segmentFlags: number[] };

/** @invariant safeInteger(this.segmentIndex) && 0 <= this.segmentIndex */
export type Cursor = { segmentIndex: number };

export function walk(prepared: Prepared, maxWidth: number): number {
  let count = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < prepared.widths.length; i++) {
    const limit = maxWidth + getProfile().epsilon;
    if (prepared.widths[i]! > limit && prepared.segmentFlags[i]! !== 0) count++;
  }
  return count;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(cursor.segmentIndex) && cursor.segmentIndex < prepared.widths.length */
export function stepped(prepared: Prepared, cursor: Cursor): number {
  const epsilon = getProfile().epsilon;
  return prepared.segmentFlags[cursor.segmentIndex]! + epsilon;
}

    // pretext's `lazyRegExp`: a factory returns a closure building its regular
// expression once, cached in a captured binding. The factory's claim states
// the returned closure's footprint, which its unit's return establishes, so
// a call of a closure it returned, held by a module constant or by an
// element of a module array, keeps the facts a call at that footprint
// keeps: the loop's reads below its bound after the calls are bounded.

export function lazyRegExp(source: string, flags: string): () => RegExp {
  let built: RegExp | null = null;
  return () => built ??= new RegExp(source, flags);
}

const letter = lazyRegExp("^\\p{L}$", "u");
const TESTS = [lazyRegExp("^\\p{M}$", "u"), lazyRegExp("^\\p{N}$", "u")];

let marked: number = 0;

/** Counts a text having the property: within `{value: any, store: keep}`. */
export function mark(text: string, property: number): void {
  if ((TESTS[property] ?? letter)().test(text)) marked += 1;
}

export function countLetters(texts: string[]): number {
  let count = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < texts.length; i++) {
    const re = letter();
    if (re.test(texts[i]!)) count += 1;
    mark(texts[i]!, 1);
    count += texts[i]!.length;
  }
  return count + marked;
}

7634dd4ba · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 11, 20:25

Specify canonical component interfaces and their replay boundary

no-behaviour-change

Why

Each importer repeats its imported modules' walks and checks. Publishing the judgments of an ordinary run of one file would admit measurement stand-ins and mismatched identities of given facts, and cache entries that refer to each other leave import cycles undefined.

modifiedDocs module-interfaces draft: the component computation, its keys and its replay boundary

Certified imports give a footprint its meaning, and stage replay its reuse at exactly the same inputs. One canonical computation per component, shared by a file's own run and by its importers, excludes measurement stand-ins, normalizes the identities of given facts to module:<location>#<unit>, checks the complete groups required and closes their dependencies before anything is published. The strongly connected components of the import graph form a DAG ordered by module location; within a component an import of a later member has the ordinary effect, so two conditional acceptances cannot establish each other. A written effect is published by the same rule as an inferred one, a successful check. The request and the process manifest bind every input that affects the result; dependencies run before the parent's claim; a failure publishes no interface. Cold, warm and concurrent costs are measured apart.

// last`, the equality is the last test and its dispatch narrows `last`.
type Kind = 0 | 1 | 2;

function kindOf(n: number): Kind {
  return n > 2 ? 2 : n > 1 ? 1 : 0;
}

function gathers(k: Kind): boolean {
  return k !== 0;
}

export function runs(n: number): number {
  let last = -1;
  let count = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const kind = kindOf(i);

    last = kind;
    count++;
  }
  return count;
}

    // A class binder typing a field and a callback's rest: `run` spreads the
// stored array into the callback, whose parameters are the array's elements.
class RestRunner<T extends readonly unknown[]> {
  args: T;
  callback: (...args: T) => number;
  constructor(args: T, callback: (...args: T) => number) {
    this.args = args;
    this.callback = callback;
  }
  set(args: T): void {
    this.args = args;
  }
  run(): number {
    return this.callback(...this.args);
  }
}

function keep(seed: number): number {
  const runner = new RestRunner(
    [seed, 2] as const,
    (x: number, y: number): number => x * 10 + y,
  );
  runner.set([seed + 1, 2] as const);
  return runner.run();
}

function pair(): number {
  const runner = new RestRunner<[string, number]>(
    ["ab", 5],
    (s: string, n: number): number => s.length + n,
  );
  return runner.run();
}

export const kept = keep(4);
export const paired = pair();

export function stable(c: boolean, a: "a", b: "b"): "a" {

export function continued(c: boolean): number {

  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i = i + x) {
    x = 2;
    if (c) {
      continue;
    }
    x = 1;
    total = total + x;
  }
  return total;
}

export function broken(c: boolean, a: "a", b: "b"): "a" {
  let y: "a" | "b" = a;
  y = a;
  while (c) {
    y = b;
    if (c) {
      y = a;
      break;
    }
    y = a;
  }
  return y;
}

    // A named closure whose parameter is wider than the element of the array it
// is passed to, here a union of which the element is one arm: it is offered
// the callback's longer signature at the element, and Lean checks its body
// there, the element within the closure's parameter.
type F = { k: "f"; n: number };
type A = { k: "a"; s: string };
type T = A | F;

export function visit(t: T): number {
  return t.k === "f" ? t.n : t.s.length;
}

export function each(calls: F[]): number {
  let total = 0;
  const go = (part: T): void => {
    total += visit(part);
  };
  calls.forEach(go);
  return total;
}

export function mapped(calls: F[]): string[] {
  const name = (t: T): string => t.k;
  return calls.map(name);
}

export function tested(calls: readonly F[]): boolean {
  const small = (t: T): boolean => visit(t) < 10;
  return calls.every(small) && calls.some(small);
}

// The element written inline, the parameter a written union of aliases.
export function inline(calls: { k: "f"; n: number }[]): number {
  let total = 0;
  const go = (part: A | F): void => {
    total += visit(part);
  };
  calls.forEach(go);
  return total;
}

// The element an alias of the union's arm, the parameter wider still.
type G = F;
export function widest(calls: G[]): string[] {
  const show = (v: T | null): string => (v === null ? "" : v.k);
  return calls.map(show);
}

// The closure changing storage: a captured array it pushes onto, and the
// mapped array itself, whose result is read with its holes.
export function collected(calls: F[]): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const add = (t: T): void => {
    out.push(t.k);
  };
  calls.forEach(add);
  return out;
}

export function shrinking(calls: F[]): (string | undefined)[] {
  const name = (t: T): string => {
    calls.pop();
    return t.k;
  };
  return calls.map(name);
}

// A guard closure wider than the element: `filter`'s guard overload.
export function present(calls: (F | null)[]): F[] {
  const isF = (t: T | null): t is F => t !== null && t.k === "f";
  return calls.filter(isF);
}

let queryFailure: unknown = null;
export function kept<T>(
  query: () => Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, T>,
): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, T> {
  try {
    return query();
  } catch (error) {

): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, number> {
  try {
    return query();
  } catch (error) {

export function nested(

  query: () => Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, number>,
): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, number> {

    return query();
  } catch (error) {
    try {
      xs.pop();
      throw error;
    } catch (second) {
      xs.pop();
      throw second;
    }
  }

export function finalizer(

): Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, number> {

    return query();
  } finally {
    queryFailure = 1;

}

  query: () => Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, number>,
): number {
  try {
    return query();
  } catch (error) {
    queryFailure = error;
    throw error;
  }

  query: () => Modifies<{ values: "any"; stores: "grow" }, number>,

// Census functions:
// type-probe.mts#nodeAt
// type-probe.mts#makeProbe
import type { Node, SourceFile } from "typescript/unstable/ast";
export function nodeAt<N extends Node>(
  file: SourceFile,
  start: number,
  end: number,
  test: (n: Node) => n is N,
): N | undefined {
  let found: N | undefined;
  const visit = (n: Node): void => {
    if (found || n.end < start || n.pos > end) return;
    const node: Node = n;
    if (test(n) && node.getStart(file) === start && node.end === end) found = n;
    else n.forEachChild(visit);
  };
  visit(file);
  return found;
}

}

declare const preparedTextBrand: unique symbol;

/**

 * @representation PreparedLineBreakData

export type PreparedText = {

};

type PreparedLineBreakData = {

type InternalPreparedText = PreparedText & PreparedLineBreakData;

export function prepare(texts: string[]): PreparedText {

7f9172b15 · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 12, 04:01

Name the kinds of change the claims-free route's records are made of

no-behaviour-change

Why

A record is a delta on the things the code implements. Of the 380 change headings in the 213 records of this branch, about 250 name a kind the format does not have: Function modified (Synthesis.lean) (80), Document (57), Script (34), Pass (14), Command, Search, Mode and twenty others. They say where the diff is, not what changed. The route's objects had no kind: a rule of the type and effect computation, an obligation of the single pass, a forced-proposal control, and a unit's agreement with the pipeline. The hook accepted any heading.

modifiedDocs review skill: the record's kinds

Three kinds are added. Proposal: a rule of the type and effect computation, written <TypeScript form> ⇒ <type or effect proposed>, with Mirrors: for the producer's rule it restates and Soundness: naming the check that refuses a wrong one. Check: an obligation acceptance depends on, written at <where>: <what must hold>. Control: a forced proposal, its unit, unforced: accepted and forced: refused at <obligation>. The list of kinds is closed, and a file, a function, a script, a command or a mode is no kind.

modifiedDocs review skill: Effect lines and sections

An Effect: line of kind agreement states a unit's verdict by the single pass before and after beside the pipeline's. Mirrors: and Validation: are named sections.

28552e3e1 · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 12, 04:09

Render proposals, checks, controls and agreement lines in review pages

no-behaviour-change

Why

The review skill adds the kinds Proposal, Check and Control, Effect: lines of kind agreement, and the sections Mirrors: and Validation:. The renderer drew the three kinds as plain prose; an agreement line promise-then-chained show@156 agreement … showed the case and unit as one name, was never expanded to the case's program, and a ⚠ after the new verdict was not marked; a range's summary did not say what kinds of change it holds.

modifiedTooling review pages: a Proposal

`<TypeScript form> ⇒ <type or effect>` drawn as a lowering line is, theform highlighted as TypeScript (a form written in backticks is thatcode), the type or effect typeset, `label: …` lines as side conditions;a paragraph with no `⇒` is prose.

modifiedTooling review pages: a Check

each `at <where>: <what must hold>` line an obligation, the place setapart and what must hold typeset, wrapped lines continuing it; Beforeand After side by side; a paragraph with no `at` line is prose.

modifiedTooling review pages: a Control

a small card: `TSCERT_FORCE=<name>` (from the block, else the heading'sobject), the unit, what it states, and `unforced accepted → forcedrefused at <obligation>` coloured as outcomes; other lines are itsstatement. `forced:<name>` in `Tests:` is drawn as a test.

modifiedTooling review pages: an agreement line

`<case> <unit>   agreement   <before> → <after>   pipeline <verdict>:<reason>`: the case, the unit, the pass's verdicts, the pipeline'sverdict coloured, the reason; the line expands to the case's programwhere the case exists; `⚠` on either verdict marks it unsound.

modifiedTooling review pages: a range's summary

the change blocks by kind, and the number of agreement lines.

Validation

A sample record with every new kind rendered and inspected in a browser; the last 120 records of the branch rendered before and after, differing only in the new kinds' drawing, forced: tests and the summary line. Mirrors: and Validation: render as named sections as Soundness: does. tools type-check; tools/unchecked.mts reports no error in these files.
